title.zh: 卷五十二 志第五 天文五
title.raw: 卷五十二 志第五 天文五 Volume 52 Treatises 5: Astronomy 5

sentences.zh: 日爲太陽之精，君之象，日行一度，一年一周天。

translations.literal: The sun is the essence of the Great Yang, the image of the ruler; the sun moves one degree a day, and in one year completes one circuit of heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The sun embodies the vital essence of the Great Yang and stands as the celestial image of the sovereign; it advances one degree each day and completes a full circuit of the heavens in a year.

sentences.zh: 日月行有道之國，則光明。

translations.literal: When the sun and moon traverse a realm governed by the Way, then they shine brightly.
translations.idiomatic: If the sun and moon pass over a kingdom ruled according to the Way, their radiance is clear and bright.

sentences.zh: 君道至大，則日色光明；

translations.literal: When the ruler's Way is at its greatest, then the sun's color is bright;
translations.idiomatic: When the sovereign's virtue reaches its height, the sun's hue grows luminous;

sentences.zh: 動不失時，則日揚光。

translations.literal: when movement does not miss its season, then the sun spreads its light.
translations.idiomatic: when his actions keep proper season, the sun flares with radiance.

sentences.zh: 至德之萌，日月如連壁。

translations.literal: At the first sprouting of supreme virtue, sun and moon are like linked jade disks.
translations.idiomatic: When supreme virtue first takes root, sun and moon appear like paired jade bi disks joined together.

sentences.zh: 君臣有道，則日含「王」字；

translations.literal: When ruler and ministers follow the Way, then the sun contains the character "king";
translations.idiomatic: When sovereign and ministers uphold the Way, the character wang appears within the solar disk;

sentences.zh: 君亮天工，則日備五色；

translations.literal: when the ruler illumines the work of Heaven, then the sun displays all five colors;
translations.idiomatic: when the ruler perfects Heaven's craft, the sun shows all five colors;

sentences.zh: 有聖人起，則日再中。

translations.literal: when a sage arises, then the sun reaches the meridian twice.
translations.idiomatic: when a sage appears, the sun crosses the meridian twice in a single day.

sentences.zh: 人君有德，日有四彗，光芒四出；

translations.literal: When the ruler possesses virtue, the sun has four cometary rays, with light streaming out in four directions;
translations.idiomatic: When the sovereign is virtuous, four cometary rays appear on the sun, their light shooting forth in every direction;

sentences.zh: 日有二彗，一年再赦。

translations.literal: When the sun has two cometary rays, there are two general amnesties in one year.
translations.idiomatic: If the sun bears two cometary rays, the realm will grant two general pardons within the year.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》視祲掌十煇之法；

translations.literal: The Zhou Rites: the Shi Jin office masters the method of the ten glow-forms;
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou assign the Jin observers the method of the ten solar glow-forms;

sentences.zh: 一曰祲，陰陽五色之氣，浸淫相侵；

translations.literal: first, called infusion: the qi of yin and yang in five colors, seeping and encroaching upon one another;
translations.idiomatic: first, "infusion": the five-colored yin-yang vapors soaking into and invading one another;

sentences.zh: 二曰象，雲氣成形象；

translations.literal: second, image: cloud vapor forming shapes;
translations.idiomatic: second, "likeness": cloud vapor taking on visible forms;

sentences.zh: 三曰鑴，日旁氣刺日；

translations.literal: third, carved: qi beside the sun piercing the sun;
translations.idiomatic: third, "carving": side vapor thrusting into the solar disk;

sentences.zh: 四曰監，雲氣臨日上；

translations.literal: fourth, oversee: cloud vapor looming upon the sun;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, "overshadow": mist resting over the sun;

sentences.zh: 五曰闇暗，謂蝕及日光脫；

translations.literal: fifth, dark eclipse: meaning eclipse and the stripping away of sunlight;
translations.idiomatic: fifth, "eclipse": occultation and the loss of solar light;

sentences.zh: 六曰瞢，不光明；

translations.literal: sixth, murk: not bright and clear;
translations.idiomatic: sixth, "murk": a dim, clouded radiance;

sentences.zh: 七曰彌，白虹貫日；

translations.literal: seventh, span: a white rainbow piercing the sun;
translations.idiomatic: seventh, "span": a pale arc running through the sun;

sentences.zh: 八曰序，謂氣若山而在日上，及冠珥背璚重疊次序在於日旁；

translations.literal: eighth, ordering: meaning qi like a mountain sitting upon the sun, and crown, aureole, back, and jade-pendant qi stacked in sequence beside the sun;
translations.idiomatic: eighth, "ordering": vapor like a peak astride the sun, or crown, aureole, back, and jade-pendant halos layered in sequence at the sun's side;

sentences.zh: 九曰隮，謂暈及虹也；

translations.literal: ninth, stair: meaning halos and rainbows;
translations.idiomatic: ninth, "stair": solar halos and rainbows;

sentences.zh: 十曰想，五色有形想。

translations.literal: tenth, thought: the five colors with imagined form.
translations.idiomatic: tenth, "thought": the five colors taking on discernible shapes.

sentences.zh: 凡黃氣環在日左右爲抱氣；

translations.literal: Whenever yellow qi encircles the sun on left and right, it is embracing qi;
translations.idiomatic: When yellow vapor rings the sun on either side, the phenomenon is called embracing qi.

sentences.zh: 居日上爲戴氣、爲冠氣；

translations.literal: when it sits above the sun, it is bearing qi or crown qi;
translations.idiomatic: when it rests above the sun, it is bearing qi or crown qi;

sentences.zh: 居日下爲承氣、爲履氣；

translations.literal: when it sits below the sun, it is receiving qi or treading qi;
translations.idiomatic: when it lies beneath the sun, it is receiving qi or treading qi;

sentences.zh: 居日下左右爲紐氣、爲纓氣。

translations.literal: when it sits below the sun on left and right, it is button qi or tassel qi.
translations.idiomatic: when it appears below the sun to left or right, it is button qi or tassel qi.

sentences.zh: 抱氣則輔臣忠，餘皆爲喜、爲得地，吉。

translations.literal: Embracing qi means the assisting ministers are loyal; the rest all signify joy and gaining territory—auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Embracing qi betokens loyal supporting ministers; the other forms all portend rejoicing and territorial gain—an auspicious sign.

sentences.zh: 一珥在日西則西軍勝，在東則東軍勝，南北亦然；

translations.literal: One aureole west of the sun means the western army is victorious; east means the eastern army is victorious; south and north are likewise;
translations.idiomatic: A single aureole west of the sun means victory for the western army; east of the sun, for the eastern army; the same rule holds for south and north;

sentences.zh: 無兵，亦有拜將。

translations.literal: even without warfare, there is also the appointing of generals.
translations.idiomatic: even if no war is underway, generals will still be appointed.

sentences.zh: 兩珥氣圜而小在日左右，主民壽考。

translations.literal: Two aureoles, round and small, on left and right of the sun: the people enjoy long life.
translations.idiomatic: Two small, round aureoles flanking the sun presage long life for the common people.

sentences.zh: 三珥色黃白，女主喜；

translations.literal: Three aureoles, yellow-white in color: the chief consort rejoices;
translations.idiomatic: Three aureoles of yellow-white hue mean joy for the empress;

sentences.zh: 純白，爲喪；

translations.literal: pure white: mourning;
translations.idiomatic: pure white: death and mourning;

sentences.zh: 赤，爲兵；

translations.literal: red: warfare;
translations.idiomatic: red: war;

sentences.zh: 青，爲疾；

translations.literal: azure: disease;
translations.idiomatic: azure: pestilence;

sentences.zh: 黑，爲水。

translations.literal: black: flood.
translations.idiomatic: black: inundation.

sentences.zh: 四珥主立侯王，有子孫喜。

translations.literal: Four aureoles mean the enfeoffment of marquises and kings, and joy in one's descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Four aureoles portend the creation of marquises and kings and rejoicing over one's posterity.

sentences.zh: 日有黃芒，君福昌；

translations.literal: When the sun has yellow rays, the ruler's fortune flourishes;
translations.idiomatic: Yellow rays on the sun mean the sovereign's blessings will prosper;

sentences.zh: 多黃輝，王政太平。

translations.literal: many yellow gleams: the king's governance is at peace.
translations.idiomatic: many yellow gleams betoken tranquil royal rule.

sentences.zh: 日無光，爲兵、喪，又爲臣有陰謀。

translations.literal: When the sun has no light, there is warfare and mourning, and also ministers harboring secret plots.
translations.idiomatic: A sun stripped of light foretells war, mourning, and ministers plotting in secret.

sentences.zh: 日旁雲氣白如席，兵衆戰死；

translations.literal: Cloud vapor beside the sun, white like a mat: many soldiers die in battle;
translations.idiomatic: Side vapor beside the sun, white as a mat, means mass death among the troops;

sentences.zh: 黑，有叛臣；

translations.literal: black: there are treacherous ministers;
translations.idiomatic: black: treacherous ministers appear;

sentences.zh: 如蛇貫之而青，穀多傷；

translations.literal: like a snake piercing through it and azure: grain suffers much damage;
translations.idiomatic: if a serpent-like vapor pierces it and the color is azure, grain crops suffer heavy loss;

sentences.zh: 白，爲兵；

translations.literal: white: warfare;
translations.idiomatic: white: war;

sentences.zh: 赤，其下有叛；

translations.literal: red: rebellion below;
translations.idiomatic: red: rebellion in the lower ranks;

sentences.zh: 黃，臣下交兵；

translations.literal: yellow: ministers and subordinates make war on one another;
translations.idiomatic: yellow: subordinate officials clash in arms;

sentences.zh: 黑，爲水。

translations.literal: black: flood.
translations.idiomatic: black: flooding.

sentences.zh: 日始出，黑雲氣貫之，三日有暴雨。

translations.literal: At the sun's first rising, black cloud vapor pierces it: within three days there is violent rain.
translations.idiomatic: If black cloud vapor runs through the sun at dawn, a torrential downpour will come within three days.

sentences.zh: 青雲在上下，可出兵。

translations.literal: Azure cloud above and below: troops may be deployed.
translations.idiomatic: Azure vapor above and below the sun permits the dispatch of armies.

sentences.zh: 有赤氣如死蛇，爲饑，爲疫。

translations.literal: Red vapor like a dead snake: famine and pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: Red vapor shaped like a dead serpent portends famine and epidemic disease.

sentences.zh: 雜氣刺日皆爲兵。

translations.literal: Mixed vapors piercing the sun are all omens of warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Any mixed side vapor thrusting into the sun is an omen of war.

sentences.zh: 日暈，七日內無風雨，亦爲兵；

translations.literal: A solar halo: if within seven days there is no wind or rain, it is also an omen of warfare;
translations.idiomatic: A solar halo: if no wind or rain follows within seven days, war is also indicated;

sentences.zh: 甲乙，憂火；

translations.literal: on jia-yi days, anxiety over fire;
translations.idiomatic: on wood days (jia and yi), fear of fire;

sentences.zh: 丙丁，臣下忠；

translations.literal: on bing-ding days, loyalty among subordinate ministers;
translations.idiomatic: on fire days (bing and ding), loyalty among the ministers;

sentences.zh: 戊己，後族盛；

translations.literal: on wu-ji days, the consort clan flourishes;
translations.idiomatic: on earth days (wu and ji), the empress's kin rise in power;

sentences.zh: 庚辛，將利；

translations.literal: on geng-xin days, generals gain advantage;
translations.idiomatic: on metal days (geng and xin), commanders prosper;

sentences.zh: 壬癸，臣專政。

translations.literal: on ren-gui days, ministers monopolize government.
translations.idiomatic: on water days (ren and gui), ministers dominate the government.

sentences.zh: 半暈，相有謀；

translations.literal: A half-halo: the chancellor harbors a plot;
translations.idiomatic: A half-halo means the chief minister is scheming;

sentences.zh: 黃，則吉；

translations.literal: yellow: then auspicious;
translations.idiomatic: if yellow, the sign is auspicious;

sentences.zh: 黑，爲災。

translations.literal: black: disaster.
translations.idiomatic: if black, calamity follows.

sentences.zh: 暈再重，歲豐；

translations.literal: A double halo: the year is abundant;
translations.idiomatic: A double halo portends a bountiful harvest;

sentences.zh: 色青，爲兵，穀貴；

translations.literal: azure in color: warfare, and grain is costly;
translations.idiomatic: if azure, war breaks out and grain grows dear;

sentences.zh: 赤，蝗爲災。

translations.literal: red: locusts bring disaster.
translations.idiomatic: if red, locust plagues devastate the land.

sentences.zh: 三重，兵起。

translations.literal: A triple halo: warfare arises.
translations.idiomatic: Three halos mean war will erupt.

sentences.zh: 四重，臣叛。

translations.literal: A quadruple halo: ministers rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Four halos mean ministerial rebellion.

sentences.zh: 五重，兵、饑。

translations.literal: A quintuple halo: warfare and famine.
translations.idiomatic: Five halos foretell war and famine.

sentences.zh: 六重，兵、喪。

translations.literal: A sextuple halo: warfare and mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Six halos mean war and death.

sentences.zh: 七重，天下亡。

translations.literal: A septuple halo: the realm perishes.
translations.idiomatic: Seven halos portend the fall of the realm.

sentences.zh: 日並出，諸侯有謀，無道用兵者亡。

translations.literal: Two suns appearing together: the feudal lords harbor designs; the one who wields arms without the Way perishes.
translations.idiomatic: When two suns appear at once, the feudal lords plot rebellion, and any ruler who resorts to force without virtue is doomed.

sentences.zh: 日辟，爲兵寇。

translations.literal: The sun splitting apart: armed invaders.
translations.idiomatic: A split sun presages invasion by armed enemies.

sentences.zh: 日隕，下失政。

translations.literal: The sun falling: loss of proper governance below.
translations.idiomatic: A falling sun means misgovernment in the lower realm.

sentences.zh: 日中見飛燕，下有廢主。

translations.literal: Swallows seen flying within the sun at midday: below there is a deposed ruler.
translations.idiomatic: If swallows are seen flying inside the sun at noon, a ruler below will be deposed.

sentences.zh: 日中黑子，臣蔽主明。

translations.literal: A black spot at the center of the sun: ministers obscure the ruler's clarity.
translations.idiomatic: A black spot at the sun's center means ministers block the sovereign's light.

sentences.zh: 日晝昏，臣蔽君之明，有篡弑。

translations.literal: The sun dim at midday: ministers obscure the ruler's clarity, and there is usurpation and regicide.
translations.idiomatic: A sun darkened at noon shows ministers eclipsing the sovereign's wisdom and foretells usurpation or assassination.

sentences.zh: 赤如血，君喪臣叛。

translations.literal: Red like blood: the ruler dies and ministers rebel.
translations.idiomatic: A blood-red sun means the sovereign perishes and his ministers turn traitor.

sentences.zh: 日夜出，兵起，下陵上，大水。

translations.literal: The sun appearing by night: warfare arises, the lower overtops the upper, and great flood.
translations.idiomatic: A sun visible at night portends war, subjects overwhelming their superiors, and catastrophic flooding.

sentences.zh: 日光四散，君失明。

translations.literal: Sunlight scattering in four directions: the ruler loses his sight.
translations.idiomatic: Sunlight radiating in all directions means the sovereign loses clear vision.

sentences.zh: 白虹貫日，近臣亂，諸侯叛。

translations.literal: A white rainbow piercing the sun: disorder among close ministers, and the feudal lords rebel.
translations.idiomatic: A white rainbow running through the sun foretells turmoil among intimate advisers and rebellion among the feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 日赤如火，君亡。

translations.literal: The sun red as fire: the ruler perishes.
translations.idiomatic: A sun red as flame means the sovereign's death.

sentences.zh: 日生牙，下有賊臣。

translations.literal: The sun sprouting tusk-like rays: below there are treacherous ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Tusk-like rays on the sun mean treacherous ministers below.

sentences.zh: 日食，爲陰蔽陽，食既則大臣憂，臣叛主，兵起。

translations.literal: A solar eclipse: yin obscures yang; if the eclipse is total, great ministers are troubled, ministers rebel against the ruler, and warfare arises.
translations.idiomatic: A solar eclipse is yin overpowering yang; at totality, high ministers are imperiled, subjects rebel against the throne, and war breaks out.

sentences.zh: 日食在正旦，王者惡之。

translations.literal: A solar eclipse at the exact dawn: the king dreads it.
translations.idiomatic: An eclipse at the very moment of dawn is deeply ominous for the king.

sentences.zh: 日珥，甲乙，日有二珥四珥而食，白雲中出，主兵；

translations.literal: Solar aureoles: on jia-yi days, if the sun has two or four aureoles and an eclipse, emerging from white clouds—warfare;
translations.idiomatic: Solar aureoles: on wood days, if the sun bears two or four aureoles and is eclipsed, with white clouds emerging from the disk, war is indicated;

sentences.zh: 丙丁，黑雲，天下疫；

translations.literal: on bing-ding days, black clouds: pestilence throughout the realm;
translations.idiomatic: on fire days, with black clouds: epidemic disease across the realm;

sentences.zh: 戊己，青雲，兵、喪；

translations.literal: on wu-ji days, azure clouds: warfare and mourning;
translations.idiomatic: on earth days, with azure clouds: war and mourning;

sentences.zh: 庚辛，赤雲，天下有少主；

translations.literal: on geng-xin days, red clouds: throughout the realm there is a young ruler;
translations.idiomatic: on metal days, with red clouds: a child sovereign reigns;

sentences.zh: 壬癸，黃雲，有土功。

translations.literal: on ren-gui days, yellow clouds: there is earthwork.
translations.idiomatic: on water days, with yellow clouds: major earthworks are undertaken.

sentences.zh: 日食在甲乙日，主四海之外，不占；

translations.literal: A solar eclipse on jia-yi days: it governs lands beyond the four seas—not to be divined;
translations.idiomatic: An eclipse on wood days affects regions beyond the four seas and is not taken into account in divination;

sentences.zh: 丙丁，江、淮、海、岱也；

translations.literal: on bing-ding days: the Yangtze, Huai, sea, and Mount Tai regions;
translations.idiomatic: on fire days: the Yangtze, Huai, coastal, and Mount Tai regions;

sentences.zh: 戊己，中州河、濟也；

translations.literal: on wu-ji days: the Central Domain, the Yellow and Ji Rivers;
translations.idiomatic: on earth days: the Central Domain and the Yellow and Ji river valleys;

sentences.zh: 庚辛，華山以西；

translations.literal: on geng-xin days: west of Mount Hua;
translations.idiomatic: on metal days: the lands west of Mount Hua;

sentences.zh: 壬癸，常山以北。

translations.literal: on ren-gui days: north of Mount Chang.
translations.idiomatic: on water days: the territory north of Mount Chang.

sentences.zh: 各以其下所主當之。

translations.literal: Each is matched against the region it governs below.
translations.idiomatic: Each day-sign is correlated with the territory it rules below.

sentences.zh: 寅卯辰木，招謀者司徒也。

translations.literal: Yin, mao, and chen—Wood: the one who draws forth the plot is the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: The yin-mao-chen hours, belonging to Wood: the Minister of Education draws forth the conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 巳午未火，招謀者太子也。

translations.literal: Si, wu, and wei—Fire: the one who draws forth the plot is the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The si-wu-wei hours, belonging to Fire: the crown prince draws forth the conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 申酉戌金，司馬也。

translations.literal: Shen, you, and xu—Metal: the Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: The shen-you-xu hours, belonging to Metal: the Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 亥子丑水，司空也。

translations.literal: Hai, zi, and chou—Water: the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: The hai-zi-chou hours, belonging to Water: the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 月爲太陰之精，女主之象，一月一周天。

translations.literal: The moon is the essence of the Great Yin, the image of the chief consort; in one month it completes one circuit of heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The moon embodies the vital essence of the Great Yin and stands as the celestial image of the empress; it completes one circuit of the heavens in a month.

sentences.zh: 君明，則依度；

translations.literal: When the ruler is enlightened, then it keeps to its measure;
translations.idiomatic: When the sovereign is wise, the moon keeps to its proper course;

sentences.zh: 臣專，則失道。

translations.literal: when ministers monopolize power, then it loses the Way.
translations.idiomatic: when ministers seize authority, it strays from its path.

sentences.zh: 或大臣用事，兵刑失理，則乍南乍北；

translations.literal: Or when great ministers hold power, military punishments fall out of order, then it suddenly shifts south and suddenly north;
translations.idiomatic: If powerful ministers dominate affairs and military justice goes awry, the moon veers abruptly south and north;

sentences.zh: 或女主外戚專權，則或進或退。

translations.literal: or when the chief consort and her kin monopolize power, then it advances or retreats.
translations.idiomatic: if the empress and her consort clan seize control, it advances or retreats erratically.

sentences.zh: 月變色，爲殃；

translations.literal: When the moon changes color, there is calamity;
translations.idiomatic: A change in the moon's color brings disaster;

sentences.zh: 青，饑；

translations.literal: azure: famine;
translations.idiomatic: azure: famine;

sentences.zh: 赤，兵、旱；

translations.literal: red: warfare and drought;
translations.idiomatic: red: war and drought;

sentences.zh: 黃，喜；

translations.literal: yellow: joy;
translations.idiomatic: yellow: rejoicing;

sentences.zh: 黑，水。

translations.literal: black: flood.
translations.idiomatic: black: inundation.

sentences.zh: 晝明，則奸邪作。

translations.literal: Bright by day: treacherous and wicked acts arise.
translations.idiomatic: If the moon shines bright in daylight, treachery and wickedness flourish.

sentences.zh: 月旁瑞氣，一珥，五穀登；

translations.literal: Auspicious qi beside the moon: one aureole—the five grains are abundant;
translations.idiomatic: Auspicious vapor beside the moon: a single aureole means a rich harvest;

sentences.zh: 兩珥，外兵勝；

translations.literal: two aureoles: external armies are victorious;
translations.idiomatic: two aureoles: foreign armies prevail;

sentences.zh: 四珥及生戴氣，君喜國安。

translations.literal: four aureoles and the appearance of bearing qi: the ruler rejoices and the state is secure.
translations.idiomatic: four aureoles together with bearing qi mean the sovereign rejoices and the realm is at peace.

sentences.zh: 終歲不暈，天下偃兵。

translations.literal: No halo throughout the year: weapons are laid down throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: If no halo appears all year, war ceases across the realm.

sentences.zh: 晦而明見西方，曰朏；

translations.literal: Bright at the last day of the month and seen in the west: this is called fei;
translations.idiomatic: Shining on the last day of the month and visible in the west is called fei;

sentences.zh: 朔而明見東方，曰仄匿。

translations.literal: bright on the first day and seen in the east: this is called ze ni.
translations.idiomatic: shining on the first day and visible in the east is called ze ni.

sentences.zh: 朏則政緩，仄匿則政急。

translations.literal: Fei means relaxed governance; ze ni means urgent governance.
translations.idiomatic: Fei portends lax administration; ze ni portends harsh administration.

sentences.zh: 六日而弦，臣專政。

translations.literal: The crescent on the sixth day: ministers monopolize government.
translations.idiomatic: A crescent appearing on the sixth day means ministers dominate the government.

sentences.zh: 七日而弦，主勝客。

translations.literal: The crescent on the seventh day: the ruler overcomes the guest.
translations.idiomatic: A crescent on the seventh day means the sovereign prevails over his adversaries.

sentences.zh: 八日而弦，天下安。

translations.literal: The crescent on the eighth day: the realm is secure.
translations.idiomatic: A crescent on the eighth day means peace throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 十日不弦，將死，戰不勝。

translations.literal: No crescent by the tenth day: generals die, and battles are not won.
translations.idiomatic: If no crescent appears by the tenth day, commanders perish and armies cannot win.

sentences.zh: 兩月並見，兵起，國亂，水溢。

translations.literal: Two moons seen together: warfare arises, the state falls into disorder, and waters overflow.
translations.idiomatic: Two moons visible at once portend war, civil chaos, and flooding.

sentences.zh: 星入月中，亡國破將。

translations.literal: A star entering the moon: the state perishes and generals are broken.
translations.idiomatic: If a star enters the moon, the kingdom falls and its generals are destroyed.

sentences.zh: 白暈貫之，下有廢主。

translations.literal: A white halo piercing through it: below there is a deposed ruler.
translations.idiomatic: A white halo running through the moon means a ruler below will be deposed.

sentences.zh: 白虹貫之，爲大兵起。

translations.literal: A white rainbow piercing it: great warfare arises.
translations.idiomatic: A white rainbow piercing the moon portends major war.

sentences.zh: 生齒，則下有叛臣。

translations.literal: It sprouts teeth: below there are rebellious ministers.
translations.idiomatic: If the moon grows tooth-like projections, rebellious ministers appear below.

sentences.zh: 生足，則後族專政。

translations.literal: It sprouts feet: the consort clan monopolizes government.
translations.idiomatic: If the moon grows foot-like projections, the empress's kin seize power.

sentences.zh: 月珥背璚，暈而珥，六十日兵起；

translations.literal: Lunar aureoles, back qi, and jade-pendant qi; a halo with aureoles: within sixty days warfare arises;
translations.idiomatic: Lunar aureoles, back qi, and jade-pendant qi; a halo accompanied by aureoles: war breaks out within sixty days;

sentences.zh: 珥青，憂；

translations.literal: aureoles azure: anxiety;
translations.idiomatic: azure aureoles: anxiety;

sentences.zh: 赤，兵；

translations.literal: red: warfare;
translations.idiomatic: red: war;

sentences.zh: 白，喪；

translations.literal: white: mourning;
translations.idiomatic: white: mourning;

sentences.zh: 黑，國亡；

translations.literal: black: the state perishes;
translations.idiomatic: black: the state falls;

sentences.zh: 黃，喜。

translations.literal: yellow: joy.
translations.idiomatic: yellow: rejoicing.

sentences.zh: 有背璚，臣下馳縱，欲相殘賊，不和之氣。

translations.literal: When there is back qi and jade-pendant qi, subordinate ministers run wild, wishing to mutilate and slay one another—the qi of discord.
translations.idiomatic: Back qi and jade-pendant qi mean subordinate ministers run rampant, bent on mutual destruction—the vapor of strife.

sentences.zh: 暈三重，兵起；

translations.literal: A triple halo: warfare arises;
translations.idiomatic: Three halos: war erupts;

sentences.zh: 四重，國亡；

translations.literal: a quadruple halo: the state perishes;
translations.idiomatic: four halos: the state falls;

sentences.zh: 五重，女主憂；

translations.literal: a quintuple halo: the chief consort is troubled;
translations.idiomatic: five halos: the empress is imperiled;

sentences.zh: 六重，國失政；

translations.literal: a sextuple halo: the state loses proper governance;
translations.idiomatic: six halos: the government falls into disorder;

sentences.zh: 七重，下易主；

translations.literal: a septuple halo: the lower realm changes its ruler;
translations.idiomatic: seven halos: the lower realm changes its sovereign;

sentences.zh: 八重，亡國；

translations.literal: an octuple halo: the state perishes;
translations.idiomatic: eight halos: the state is destroyed;

sentences.zh: 九重，兵起亡地；

translations.literal: a nonuple halo: warfare arises and territory is lost;
translations.idiomatic: nine halos: war breaks out and territory is lost;

sentences.zh: 十重，天下更始。

translations.literal: a decuple halo: the realm begins anew.
translations.idiomatic: ten halos: the realm is remade.

sentences.zh: 月食，從上始則君失道，從旁始爲相失令，從下始爲將失法。

translations.literal: A lunar eclipse: if it begins from above, the ruler loses the Way; if from the side, the chancellor loses his command; if from below, the general loses discipline.
translations.idiomatic: In a lunar eclipse, if shadow enters from above, the sovereign strays from the Way; from the side, the chancellor misgoverns; from below, the general breaks discipline.

sentences.zh: 歲星犯之，兵、饑、民流。

translations.literal: When Jupiter transgresses it: warfare, famine, and the people scatter.
translations.idiomatic: If Jupiter transgresses the moon, war, famine, and mass displacement follow.

sentences.zh: 熒惑犯之，大將死，有叛臣，民饑。

translations.literal: When Mars transgresses it: the great general dies, there are rebellious ministers, and the people suffer famine.
translations.idiomatic: If Mars transgresses the moon, the commander-in-chief dies, traitorous ministers arise, and the people go hungry.

sentences.zh: 填星犯之，人臣弑主；

translations.literal: When Saturn transgresses it: a minister assassinates the ruler;
translations.idiomatic: If Saturn transgresses the moon, a minister slays the sovereign;

sentences.zh: 合，國饑。

translations.literal: conjunction: the state suffers famine.
translations.idiomatic: conjunction: famine afflicts the realm.

sentences.zh: 月食填星，民流；

translations.literal: A lunar eclipse with Saturn: the people scatter;
translations.idiomatic: A lunar eclipse involving Saturn: the people disperse;

sentences.zh: 一曰月犯填，女主憂，民流。

translations.literal: one account says: when the moon transgresses Saturn, the chief consort is troubled and the people scatter.
translations.idiomatic: another tradition holds: when the moon transgresses Saturn, the empress is imperiled and the people flee.

sentences.zh: 太白犯，出月右爲陰國有謀，左爲陽國有謀；

translations.literal: When Venus transgresses it: emerging to the right of the moon means the yin realm harbors a plot; to the left means the yang realm harbors a plot;
translations.idiomatic: If Venus transgresses the moon: appearing to the moon's right means the northern/yin states plot rebellion; to the left, the southern/yang states;

sentences.zh: 出月下，君死、民流。

translations.literal: emerging below the moon: the ruler dies and the people scatter.
translations.idiomatic: appearing below the moon: the sovereign dies and the people are displaced.

sentences.zh: 月戴太白，起兵；

translations.literal: The moon bearing Venus: warfare arises;
translations.idiomatic: The moon crowned with Venus: war breaks out;

sentences.zh: 入月，將死；

translations.literal: entering the moon: the general dies;
translations.idiomatic: entering the moon: the general perishes;

sentences.zh: 與太白會，太子危。

translations.literal: meeting with Venus: the heir apparent is imperiled.
translations.idiomatic: conjunction with Venus: the crown prince is in danger.

sentences.zh: 辰星犯之，天下水。

translations.literal: When Mercury transgresses it: flood throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: If Mercury transgresses the moon, flooding spreads across the realm.

sentences.zh: 月食辰，水，饑。

translations.literal: A lunar eclipse with Mercury: flood and famine.
translations.idiomatic: A lunar eclipse involving Mercury: flood and famine.

sentences.zh: 辰入月，臣叛主。

translations.literal: Mercury entering the moon: ministers rebel against the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Mercury entering the moon: ministers rebel against the throne.

sentences.zh: 彗星入，或犯之，兵期十二年，大饑；

translations.literal: A comet entering, or transgressing it: warfare within twelve years, and great famine;
translations.idiomatic: A comet entering the moon or transgressing it: war within twelve years and severe famine;

sentences.zh: 貫月，臣叛主。

translations.literal: piercing the moon: ministers rebel against the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: piercing through the moon: ministers rebel against the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 流星犯之，有兵；

translations.literal: A meteor transgressing it: there is warfare;
translations.idiomatic: A meteor transgressing the moon: war;

sentences.zh: 入無光，有亡國；

translations.literal: entering without light: a state perishes;
translations.idiomatic: entering and extinguishing its light: a kingdom falls;

sentences.zh: 在月上下，國將亂。

translations.literal: above or below the moon: the state will fall into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: above or below the moon: the realm descends into chaos.

sentences.zh: 月犯列星，其國受兵。

translations.literal: When the moon transgresses the fixed stars, that state receives warfare.
translations.idiomatic: If the moon transgresses a fixed star, the corresponding state suffers attack.

sentences.zh: 星食月，國相死。

translations.literal: A star eclipsing the moon: the state's chancellor dies.
translations.idiomatic: If a star eclipses the moon, that state's chief minister dies.

sentences.zh: 星見月中，主憂。

translations.literal: A star appearing within the moon: the ruler is troubled.
translations.idiomatic: A star visible inside the moon: the sovereign is imperiled.

sentences.zh: 凡月之行，曆二十有九日五十三分而輿日相會，是謂合朔。

translations.literal: In general, the moon's motion, over twenty-nine days and fifty-three parts, meets the sun in its carriage—this is called new moon conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: As a rule, the moon completes twenty-nine days and fifty-three parts before meeting the sun again—this is termed new moon conjunction.

sentences.zh: 當朔日之交，月行黃道而日爲月所掩，則日食，是爲陰勝陽，其變重，自古聖人畏之。

translations.literal: At the crossing of the new-moon day, the moon travels the ecliptic and the sun is obscured by the moon—then there is a solar eclipse; this is yin overcoming yang, a grave transformation, which the sages of old feared.
translations.idiomatic: At new moon, if the moon travels the ecliptic and covers the sun, a solar eclipse occurs—yin overpowering yang, a weighty omen that sages since antiquity have dreaded.

sentences.zh: 若日月同度於朔，月行不入黃道，則雖會而不食。

translations.literal: If sun and moon share the same degree at new moon, yet the moon's path does not enter the ecliptic, then though they meet, there is no eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: If sun and moon align at new moon but the moon's path misses the ecliptic, they conjoin without eclipse.

sentences.zh: 月之行在望與日對沖，月入於闇虛之內，則月爲之食，是爲陽勝陰，其變輕。

translations.literal: The moon's motion at full moon stands opposite the sun; the moon enters within the shadow cone, and the moon is eclipsed—this is yang overcoming yin, a lighter transformation.
translations.idiomatic: At full moon the moon stands opposite the sun; entering the shadow cone, it is eclipsed—yang overpowering yin, a lesser transformation.

sentences.zh: 昔朱熹謂月食終亦爲災，陰若退避，則不至相敵而食。

translations.literal: Formerly Zhu Xi said that even when a lunar eclipse ends, it is still a calamity; if yin retreats and yields, then the two will not reach mutual opposition and eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi once observed that even a lunar eclipse ending in recovery remains ominous; only if yin withdraws and yields will the two bodies fail to meet in opposition and eclipse.

sentences.zh: 所謂闇虛，蓋日火外明，其對必有闇氣，大小與日體同。

translations.literal: What is called the shadow cone: the sun's fire is bright without, and opposite it there must be dark vapor, its size the same as the solar body.
translations.idiomatic: The so-called shadow cone arises because the sun's fire is bright on the outside; directly opposite must lie dark vapor equal in size to the solar disk.

sentences.zh: 此日月交會薄食之大略也。

translations.literal: This is the great outline of solar and lunar conjunction and partial eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: These are the principal outlines of solar and lunar conjunction and partial eclipse.

sentences.zh: 日食修德，月食修刑，自昔人主遇災而懼，側身修行者，此也。

translations.literal: At a solar eclipse cultivate virtue; at a lunar eclipse refine punishments—from old, when rulers encountered calamities and were afraid, they turned inward in self-cultivation; this is the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Solar eclipses call for moral cultivation; lunar eclipses for refining punishments—since antiquity, rulers who feared such omens turned inward to reform themselves; this is why.

sentences.zh: 歲星爲東方，爲春，爲木。

translations.literal: Jupiter is the east, spring, and wood.
translations.idiomatic: Jupiter governs the east, spring, and the element wood.

sentences.zh: 于人五常，仁也；

translations.literal: Among the five constant virtues in man, it is benevolence;
translations.idiomatic: Among the five human virtues, it corresponds to benevolence;

sentences.zh: 五事，貌也。

translations.literal: among the five affairs, it is appearance.
translations.idiomatic: among the five governmental affairs, it corresponds to personal bearing.

sentences.zh: 超舍而前爲贏，退舍爲縮。

translations.literal: Advancing beyond its lodge is called surging ahead; retreating from its lodge is called lagging behind.
translations.idiomatic: Moving ahead of its calculated lodge is termed surging ahead; falling back from its lodge is termed lagging behind.

sentences.zh: 色光明潤，君壽民富。

translations.literal: Its color bright, luminous, and moist: the ruler enjoys long life and the people are wealthy.
translations.idiomatic: When its color is bright, lustrous, and moist, the sovereign lives long and the people prosper.

sentences.zh: 又主福，主大司農，主五穀。

translations.literal: It also governs fortune, the Grand Minister of Agriculture, and the five grains.
translations.idiomatic: It also presides over good fortune, the Grand Minister of Agriculture, and the harvest of the five grains.

sentences.zh: 石申曰：歲星所在，國不可伐，如歲在卯，不可東征。

translations.literal: Shi Shen says: Where Jupiter stands, that state must not be attacked; as when the year-star is in mao, one must not campaign eastward.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Shen says: The state where Jupiter resides must not be attacked—for example, when Jupiter is in mao, no eastern campaign should be launched.

sentences.zh: 甘德曰：所去，國凶；

translations.literal: Gan De says: The state it leaves is inauspicious;
translations.idiomatic: Gan De says: The state Jupiter departs from meets misfortune;

sentences.zh: 所之，國吉；

translations.literal: the state it goes to is auspicious;
translations.idiomatic: the state it enters enjoys good fortune;

sentences.zh: 退行，爲凶災。

translations.literal: retrograde motion: inauspicious calamity.
translations.idiomatic: retrograde motion brings dire calamity.

sentences.zh: 主泰山、徐青兗及角、亢、氐、房、心、尾、箕。

translations.literal: It governs Mount Tai, Xu, Qing, Yan, and the lodges Horn, Neck, Root, Room, Heart, Tail, and Winnowing Basket.
translations.idiomatic: It presides over Mount Tai and the regions of Xu, Qing, and Yan, and over the lodges Horn, Neck, Root, Room, Heart, Tail, and Winnowing Basket.

sentences.zh: 君令不順，則歲星退行；

translations.literal: When the ruler's commands are not compliant, then Jupiter moves in retrograde;
translations.idiomatic: When the sovereign's orders go unheeded, Jupiter turns retrograde;

sentences.zh: 入陰爲內事，入陽爲外事；

translations.literal: entering yin: internal affairs; entering yang: external affairs;
translations.idiomatic: entering the yin half of the sky: domestic affairs; entering the yang half: foreign affairs;

sentences.zh: 行陰道爲水，行陽道爲旱。

translations.literal: traveling the yin path: flood; traveling the yang path: drought.
translations.idiomatic: moving along the yin path: flooding; along the yang path: drought.

sentences.zh: 星大，則喜；

translations.literal: When the star is large: joy;
translations.idiomatic: When the planet appears large: rejoicing;

sentences.zh: 小，則牛馬多死，疾疫。

translations.literal: small: many cattle and horses die, and pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: when small: mass death among cattle and horses, and epidemic disease.

sentences.zh: 初見小而日益大，所居國利。

translations.literal: At first appearance small and daily growing larger: the state where it dwells benefits.
translations.idiomatic: If it first appears small and grows larger each day, the state it occupies prospers.

sentences.zh: 初出大而日小，國耗。

translations.literal: At first emergence large and daily growing smaller: the state is depleted.
translations.idiomatic: If it first emerges large and shrinks daily, that state is drained.

sentences.zh: 《荊州占》：歲星色黑，爲喪；

translations.literal: Jingzhou Prognostications: When Jupiter's color is black, there is mourning;
translations.idiomatic: The Jingzhou Prognostications state: When Jupiter is black, mourning follows;

sentences.zh: 黃，則歲豐；

translations.literal: yellow: then the year is abundant;
translations.idiomatic: yellow: a bountiful year;

sentences.zh: 白，爲兵；

translations.literal: white: warfare;
translations.idiomatic: white: war;

sentences.zh: 青，多獄；

translations.literal: azure: many prisons;
translations.idiomatic: azure: crowded prisons;

sentences.zh: 君暴，則色赤。

translations.literal: when the ruler is violent, then the color is red.
translations.idiomatic: when the sovereign is tyrannical, its color turns red.

sentences.zh: 熒惑相犯，爲大戰；

translations.literal: Mutual transgression with Mars: great battle;
translations.idiomatic: Mutual transgression with Mars: major war;

sentences.zh: 相去方寸爲犯，戰，客勝。

translations.literal: separated by a cun or so is transgression: battle, and the guest is victorious.
translations.idiomatic: standing a few minutes of arc apart counts as transgression: war, and the invader prevails.

sentences.zh: 食火，國亡。

translations.literal: Eclipsing fire: the state perishes.
translations.idiomatic: Obscuring Mars: the state is destroyed.

sentences.zh: 邊侵曰食。

translations.literal: Border encroachment is called eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Partial overlap at the edge is termed eclipse.

sentences.zh: 守之爲賊。

translations.literal: Stationing upon it means banditry.
translations.idiomatic: Stationing upon Mars signifies banditry.

sentences.zh: 居之不去爲守。

translations.literal: Dwelling there without departing is called stationing.
translations.idiomatic: Remaining in place without moving on is called stationing.

sentences.zh: 觸火，則國亂。

translations.literal: Striking fire: then the state falls into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Striking Mars: the realm descends into chaos.

sentences.zh: 兩體俱動而直曰觸。

translations.literal: Both bodies moving and meeting straight on is called striking.
translations.idiomatic: When both bodies are in motion and meet head-on, the phenomenon is called striking.

sentences.zh: 合鬥，爲饑、旱。

translations.literal: Conjunction and combat: famine and drought.
translations.idiomatic: When planets join in combat, the omen is famine and drought.

sentences.zh: 離復合、合復離曰鬥。

translations.literal: Separating and rejoining, or joining and separating again, is called combat.
translations.idiomatic: When two bodies part and meet again, or meet and part again, the phenomenon is termed combat.

sentences.zh: 填星相犯，退，犯填，太子叛。

translations.literal: When interacting with Saturn, retrograding, and encroaching upon Saturn, the heir apparent rebels.
translations.idiomatic: If Jupiter transgresses Saturn, turns retrograde, and transgresses Saturn again, the crown prince will rebel.

sentences.zh: 當東反西曰退。

translations.literal: When it should move east but turns west, it is called retrograde motion.
translations.idiomatic: Turning westward when it ought to advance eastward is called retrograde motion.

sentences.zh: 與填星合，爲內亂，民饑。

translations.literal: Conjoining with Saturn: internal disorder and the people suffer famine.
translations.idiomatic: When it conjoins with Saturn, internal rebellion arises and the people go hungry.

sentences.zh: 芒角相及同光曰合。

translations.literal: When rayed horns meet and their light merges, it is called conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: If their horned rays touch and shine as one, the event is called conjunction.

sentences.zh: 守填星，其下城敗。

translations.literal: Stationing at Saturn: the city below is defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When it stations upon Saturn, the city beneath that quarter falls.

sentences.zh: 太白相犯，大臣黜，女主喪。

translations.literal: Mutual transgression with Venus: great ministers are dismissed and the chief consort dies.
translations.idiomatic: When Jupiter and Venus mutually transgress, high ministers are removed and the empress meets death.

sentences.zh: 觸太白，則四邊來侵。

translations.literal: Striking Venus: invaders come from all four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: If it strikes Venus, enemies press in from every side.

sentences.zh: 守太白，爲四序不調。

translations.literal: Stationing at Venus: the four seasons fall out of harmony.
translations.idiomatic: When it stations at Venus, the four seasons lose their proper order.

sentences.zh: 合鬥，則大將死。

translations.literal: Conjunction and combat: the great general dies.
translations.idiomatic: If they join in combat, the commander-in-chief perishes.

sentences.zh: 辰星相犯，太子憂。

translations.literal: Mutual transgression with Mercury: the heir apparent is troubled.
translations.idiomatic: When Jupiter and Mercury mutually transgress, the crown prince is beset with anxiety.

sentences.zh: 觸辰，主憂；

translations.literal: Striking Mercury: the ruler is troubled;
translations.idiomatic: If it strikes Mercury, the sovereign is filled with worry;

sentences.zh: 守，憂賊。

translations.literal: stationing: anxiety of bandits.
translations.idiomatic: if it stations there, the fear is of brigands.

sentences.zh: 合，則君臣和。

translations.literal: Conjunction: ruler and ministers are harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: When they conjoin, ruler and ministers live in accord.

sentences.zh: 晝見，則臣強。

translations.literal: Visible by day: ministers grow powerful.
translations.idiomatic: If it appears in daylight, the ministers gain in strength.

sentences.zh: 他星犯之，主不安。

translations.literal: Other stars transgress it: the ruler is unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: When other stars encroach upon it, the sovereign cannot rest secure.

sentences.zh: 客星犯守，主憂。

translations.literal: Guest stars transgress or station upon it: the ruler is troubled.
translations.idiomatic: If guest stars transgress or station upon it, the ruler is filled with care.

sentences.zh: 流星犯之，色蒼黑，大農死；

translations.literal: Meteors transgress it: if the color is dark black, the Grand Minister of Agriculture dies;
translations.idiomatic: When a meteor strikes it, a dusky black hue means the Grand Minister of Agriculture will die;

sentences.zh: 赤，爲饑疫；

translations.literal: red: famine and pestilence;
translations.idiomatic: if red, famine and epidemic disease follow;

sentences.zh: 黃，則歲豐。

translations.literal: yellow: the year is abundant.
translations.idiomatic: if yellow, the harvest will be plentiful.

sentences.zh: 抵之，臣叛主。

translations.literal: Reaching against it: ministers rebel against the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: If a body presses directly against it, ministers rise in rebellion against their lord.

sentences.zh: 熒惑爲南方，爲夏，爲火。

translations.literal: The Sparkling Deluder is the south, summer, and fire.
translations.idiomatic: Mars presides over the south, the season of summer, and the element of fire.

sentences.zh: 于人五常，禮也；

translations.literal: Among the five constant virtues in man, it is propriety;
translations.idiomatic: In human affairs it corresponds to the virtue of ritual propriety;

sentences.zh: 五事，視也。

translations.literal: among the five affairs, it is vision.
translations.idiomatic: among the five governmental concerns, it governs the power of sight.

sentences.zh: 晉灼曰：「常以十月入太微，受制而出，行列宿，司無道，出入無常。」

translations.literal: Jin Zhuo says: "It regularly enters the Supreme Palace in the tenth month, emerges when subdued, files through the lodges, oversees the wayless, and its emergence and withdrawal are without regularity."
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhuo writes: "Mars habitually enters the Supreme Palace in the tenth month, emerges once it is constrained, marches in ranks through the lodges, supervises those who lack the Way, and its appearances and disappearances follow no fixed rule."

sentences.zh: 二歲一周天。

translations.literal: It completes one circuit of heaven in two years.
translations.idiomatic: It completes one revolution of the heavens in two years.

sentences.zh: 出，則有兵；

translations.literal: When it emerges, there is warfare;
translations.idiomatic: When Mars emerges, armies take the field;

sentences.zh: 入，則兵散。

translations.literal: when it enters, armies disperse.
translations.idiomatic: when it withdraws, the hosts break up and disperse.

sentences.zh: 逆行一舍二舍，爲不祥，所舍國爲亂、賊、疾、喪、饑、兵。

translations.literal: Retrograde motion through one or two lodges is inauspicious; the state beneath the lodge it occupies suffers disorder, banditry, disease, mourning, famine, and war.
translations.idiomatic: If it retrogrades one or two lodges, the omen is dire: the country over which that lodge presides will know rebellion, robbery, pestilence, bereavement, hunger, and war.

sentences.zh: 或環繞勾巳，芒角、動搖、變色，乍前乍後，爲殃愈甚。

translations.literal: Or if it loops around Gouchen, shows horned rays, trembles, changes color, and now advances and now retreats, the calamity grows worse still.
translations.idiomatic: Should it wheel about Gouchen, flare with horned rays, quiver, shift hue, and lurch forward and back, the disaster becomes all the more severe.

sentences.zh: 退行一舍，天下有火災；

translations.literal: Retrograde motion through one lodge: fire disasters throughout the realm;
translations.idiomatic: One lodge of retrograde motion portends conflagrations across the land;

sentences.zh: 五舍，大臣叛。

translations.literal: five lodges: great ministers rebel.
translations.idiomatic: five lodges: high ministers turn traitor.

sentences.zh: 《星經》曰：「主霍山、揚、荊、交州，又主輿鬼、柳、七星。」

translations.literal: The Star Classic says: "It presides over Mount Huo, Yang, Jing, and Jiaozhou, and also over the lodges Ghost, Willow, and the Seven Stars."
translations.idiomatic: The Star Classic states: "It governs Mount Huo, the regions of Yang, Jing, and Jiaozhou, and likewise the lodges Ghost, Willow, and the Seven Stars."

sentences.zh: 又主大鴻臚，又曰主司空，爲司馬，主楚、吳、越以南，司天下君臣之過失。

translations.literal: It also presides over the Grand Herald, and is also said to preside over the Minister of Works; as Marshal it governs Chu, Wu, Yue, and all lands to the south, and oversees the faults of ruler and ministers throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: It also rules the office of Grand Herald, is further identified with the Minister of Works, and as Marshal watches over Chu, Wu, Yue, and the south, judging the failings of sovereign and subject under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 東行，則兵聚東方；

translations.literal: Moving eastward: armies gather in the east;
translations.idiomatic: When it travels east, forces mass in the east;

sentences.zh: 西行，則兵聚西方。

translations.literal: moving westward: armies gather in the west.
translations.idiomatic: when it travels west, forces mass in the west.

sentences.zh: 天下安，則行疾。

translations.literal: When the realm is at peace, it moves swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: If the empire is tranquil, Mars hurries on its course.

sentences.zh: 與歲星相犯，主冊太子，有赦。

translations.literal: Mutual transgression with Jupiter: the ruler invests the crown prince, and there is an amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: When Mars and Jupiter mutually transgress, the sovereign enfeoffs the heir apparent and proclaims a general pardon.

sentences.zh: 觸歲星，有子；

translations.literal: Striking Jupiter: there will be a son;
translations.idiomatic: If it strikes Jupiter, an heir is born;

sentences.zh: 守之，太子危。

translations.literal: stationing upon it: the crown prince is imperiled.
translations.idiomatic: if it stations there, the crown prince stands in peril.

sentences.zh: 填星相犯，兵大起。

translations.literal: Mutual transgression with Saturn: warfare rises on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: When Mars and Saturn mutually transgress, war erupts on a vast scale.

sentences.zh: 入填星，將爲亂；

translations.literal: Entering Saturn: generals will rebel;
translations.idiomatic: If it enters Saturn, commanders will turn to rebellion;

sentences.zh: 觸之，有刀兵；

translations.literal: striking it: there is edged warfare;
translations.idiomatic: if it strikes Saturn, blades are drawn in battle;

sentences.zh: 守之，有內賊，太子危。

translations.literal: stationing upon it: there are internal traitors, and the crown prince is imperiled.
translations.idiomatic: if it stations there, traitors arise within, and the crown prince is endangered.

sentences.zh: 與太白相犯，主亡，兵起；

translations.literal: Mutual transgression with Venus: the ruler perishes and armies rise;
translations.idiomatic: When Mars and Venus mutually transgress, the sovereign dies and armies take the field;

sentences.zh: 守北，太子憂；

translations.literal: stationing to the north: the crown prince is troubled;
translations.idiomatic: if it stations to the north, the heir apparent is filled with care;

sentences.zh: 南，庶子憂。

translations.literal: to the south: the secondary sons are troubled.
translations.idiomatic: if to the south, the lesser princes are troubled.

sentences.zh: 環繞，偏將死。

translations.literal: Encircling it: a lieutenant general dies.
translations.idiomatic: If it loops around Venus, a deputy commander perishes.

sentences.zh: 與辰星相犯，兵敗。

translations.literal: Mutual transgression with Mercury: armies are defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When Mars and Mercury mutually transgress, armies meet defeat.

sentences.zh: 與辰星相會，爲旱，秋爲兵，冬爲喪；

translations.literal: Meeting Mercury: drought; in autumn, war; in winter, mourning;
translations.idiomatic: When Mars meets Mercury, drought follows; in autumn there is war, in winter bereavement;

sentences.zh: 守之，太子憂，有赦。

translations.literal: stationing upon it: the crown prince is troubled, and there is an amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: if it stations there, the crown prince is anxious, yet an amnesty is proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 他星相犯，兵起，祅星犯之，爲兵，爲火。

translations.literal: Other stars mutually transgress: armies rise; if a malefic star transgresses, there is war and fire.
translations.idiomatic: When other stars transgress Mars, war begins; if a malefic star strikes it, there is warfare and fire.

sentences.zh: 填星爲中央，爲季夏，爲土。

translations.literal: The Emplacement Star is the center, late summer, and earth.
translations.idiomatic: Saturn presides over the center, the season of late summer, and the element of earth.

sentences.zh: 于人五常，信也；

translations.literal: Among the five constant virtues in man, it is faith;
translations.idiomatic: In human affairs it corresponds to the virtue of trustworthiness;

sentences.zh: 五事，思也。

translations.literal: among the five affairs, it is thought.
translations.idiomatic: among the five governmental concerns, it governs the power of reflection.

sentences.zh: 常以甲辰元始之歲填行一宿，二十八歲而一周天。

translations.literal: Beginning in the inaugural year of the jiachen cycle, it advances one lodge each year and completes one circuit of heaven in twenty-eight years.
translations.idiomatic: From the founding year of the jiachen sequence, Saturn moves through one lodge per year and completes a full circuit of the heavens in twenty-eight years.

sentences.zh: 四星皆失，填爲之動。

translations.literal: When all four other stars lose their places, Saturn is stirred into motion.
translations.idiomatic: When the other four planets all stray from their courses, Saturn is set in motion.

sentences.zh: 所居，國吉，女子有福，不可伐。

translations.literal: Where it dwells, the state is fortunate, women receive blessing, and it may not be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: The country over which it rests is blessed, women gain good fortune, and no foe should attack it.

sentences.zh: 去之，失地。

translations.literal: When it departs, territory is lost.
translations.idiomatic: When Saturn moves away, lands are forfeited.

sentences.zh: 天子失信，則填大動。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven loses faith, Saturn stirs greatly.
translations.idiomatic: If the sovereign breaks faith, Saturn quakes violently in its course.

sentences.zh: 盈則超舍，以德盈則加福，刑盈則不復；

translations.literal: When full it overshoots its lodge; if virtue overflows, blessing is added, but if punishment overflows it does not return;
translations.idiomatic: When swollen it leaps beyond its lodge: overflowing virtue brings added grace, but overflowing punishment means it will not resume its place;

sentences.zh: 縮則退舍不及常，德宿則迫戚，刑縮則不育。

translations.literal: when shrunken it falls short of its lodge; if virtue is cramped, sorrow presses close, and if punishment is shrunken, nothing can be nurtured.
translations.idiomatic: when contracted it falls short of its lodge: cramped virtue brings anguish, and shrunken punishment means nothing can flourish.

sentences.zh: 《星經》曰：「主嵩山、豫州，又主東井。」

translations.literal: The Star Classic says: "It presides over Mount Song and Yuzhou, and also over the Well lodge."
translations.idiomatic: The Star Classic states: "It governs Mount Song and Yuzhou, and also the lodge Well."

sentences.zh: 行中道，則陰陽和調。

translations.literal: Traveling the central path, yin and yang are harmoniously adjusted.
translations.idiomatic: When it keeps to the middle way, yin and yang fall into balance.

sentences.zh: 退行一舍，爲水；

translations.literal: Retrograde motion through one lodge: floods;
translations.idiomatic: One lodge of retrograde motion portends inundation;

sentences.zh: 二舍，海溢河決。

translations.literal: two lodges: the sea overflows and rivers burst their banks.
translations.idiomatic: two lodges: seas surge and rivers break their dikes.

sentences.zh: 經天退行，天下更政，地動。

translations.literal: Crossing the meridian while retrograde: the realm changes its government, and the earth quakes.
translations.idiomatic: If it crosses the meridian in retrograde motion, the government of the empire is overturned and the earth trembles.

sentences.zh: 巫咸曰：光明，歲熟。

translations.literal: Wu Xian says: when bright, the year is ripe.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xian writes: when Saturn shines brightly, the harvest ripens.

sentences.zh: 大明，主昌。

translations.literal: Great brightness: the ruler flourishes.
translations.idiomatic: If exceedingly bright, the sovereign prospers.

sentences.zh: 小暗，主憂。

translations.literal: Small and dim: the ruler is troubled.
translations.idiomatic: If small and faint, the sovereign is beset with care.

sentences.zh: 春青，夏赤，女主喜。

translations.literal: Green in spring, red in summer: the chief consort rejoices.
translations.idiomatic: Green in spring and red in summer mean the empress is glad.

sentences.zh: 春色蒼，歲大熟；

translations.literal: Dark green in spring: the year is greatly abundant;
translations.idiomatic: A deep green hue in spring foretells a bountiful harvest;

sentences.zh: 色赤，饑。

translations.literal: red color: famine.
translations.idiomatic: a red cast means hunger.

sentences.zh: 有芒，兵。

translations.literal: Horned rays: war.
translations.idiomatic: If it shows horned rays, war follows.

sentences.zh: 與歲星相犯相鬥，爲內亂；

translations.literal: Mutual transgression and combat with Jupiter: internal disorder;
translations.idiomatic: When Saturn transgresses or fights Jupiter, rebellion stirs within;

sentences.zh: 合，則野有兵。

translations.literal: conjunction: armies in the wild.
translations.idiomatic: if they conjoin, armies march in the open country.

sentences.zh: 熒惑相犯，爲兵、喪；

translations.literal: Mutual transgression with Mars: war and mourning;
translations.idiomatic: When Saturn and Mars mutually transgress, there is war and mourning;

sentences.zh: 合，則爲兵，爲內亂，大人忌之。

translations.literal: conjunction: war and internal disorder, and great men dread the omen.
translations.idiomatic: if they conjoin, war and civil strife arise, and men of rank look upon it with dread.

sentences.zh: 太白相犯，爲內兵，有大戰，一曰王者失地。

translations.literal: Mutual transgression with Venus: internal warfare, a great battle, and one tradition says the king loses his lands.
translations.idiomatic: When Saturn and Venus mutually transgress, civil war erupts and a great battle is fought; one account adds that the king forfeits his territory.

sentences.zh: 合於太微，國有大兵，一曰國亡。

translations.literal: Conjoining within the Supreme Palace: the state knows great war, and one tradition says the state perishes.
translations.idiomatic: If they conjoin in the Supreme Palace, the realm suffers great war; one account says the state is destroyed.

sentences.zh: 辰星犯，爲兵，爲旱。

translations.literal: Mercury transgresses: war and drought.
translations.idiomatic: When Mercury transgresses Saturn, war and drought follow.

sentences.zh: 祅星犯，下臣謀上。

translations.literal: A malefic star transgresses: subordinate ministers plot against their superiors.
translations.idiomatic: If a malefic star strikes it, lesser officials conspire against their betters.

sentences.zh: 流星犯，則民多事。

translations.literal: Meteors transgress: the people are burdened with many troubles.
translations.idiomatic: When meteors strike Saturn, the common people are weighed down with countless cares.

sentences.zh: 與月相犯，有兵。

translations.literal: Mutual transgression with the moon: there is war.
translations.idiomatic: When Saturn and the moon mutually transgress, armies take the field.

sentences.zh: 太白爲西方，爲秋，爲金。

translations.literal: The Great White is the west, autumn, and metal.
translations.idiomatic: Venus presides over the west, the season of autumn, and the element of metal.

sentences.zh: 于人五常，義也；

translations.literal: Among the five constant virtues in man, it is righteousness;
translations.idiomatic: In human affairs it corresponds to the virtue of righteousness;

sentences.zh: 五事，言也。

translations.literal: among the five affairs, it is speech.
translations.idiomatic: among the five governmental concerns, it governs the power of speech.

sentences.zh: 常以正月甲寅與火晨出東方，二百四十日而入。

translations.literal: Regularly on the first day of the first month in the jiayin sequence it emerges with Mars in the morning in the east, and after two hundred forty days it sets.
translations.idiomatic: It habitually rises with Mars in the eastern dawn on jiayin day in the first month, remains visible for two hundred forty days, and then sets.

sentences.zh: 入四十日又出西方，二百四十日而入。

translations.literal: After forty days of setting it emerges again in the west, and after two hundred forty days it sets once more.
translations.idiomatic: Forty days after setting it appears again in the west, stays two hundred forty days, and sets again.

sentences.zh: 入三十五日而復出東方。

translations.literal: After thirty-five days of setting it re-emerges in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-five days after setting it rises once more in the east.

sentences.zh: 出以寅戌，入以丑未也。

translations.literal: It emerges at yin and xu, and sets at chou and wei.
translations.idiomatic: It rises at the hours yin and xu and sets at chou and wei.

sentences.zh: 一年一周天。

translations.literal: One year completes one circuit of heaven.
translations.idiomatic: It completes one revolution of the heavens in a year.

sentences.zh: 日方南太白居其南，日方北太白居其北，爲贏，侯王不寧，用兵進吉退凶。

translations.literal: When the sun is due south and Venus stands south of it, or when the sun is due north and Venus stands north of it, this is called winning; marquis-kings are unsettled, and in warfare advance is auspicious while retreat is ill-omened.
translations.idiomatic: If the sun stands at its southern limit and Venus lies south of it, or the sun at its northern limit with Venus to the north, the configuration is called winning: feudal lords grow restless, and in battle to advance brings good fortune while to withdraw brings disaster.

sentences.zh: 日方南太白居其北，日方北太白居其南，爲縮，侯王有憂，用兵退吉進凶。

translations.literal: When the sun is due south and Venus stands north of it, or when the sun is due north and Venus stands south of it, this is called contracting; marquis-kings have cause for worry, and in warfare retreat is auspicious while advance is ill-omened.
translations.idiomatic: If the sun is south and Venus north, or the sun north and Venus south, the configuration is called contracting: feudal lords are filled with anxiety, and in battle retreat is lucky while advance is ruinous.

sentences.zh: 《星經》曰：「主華陰山、梁、雍、益州，又主奎、婁、胃、昴、畢、觜、參。」

translations.literal: The Star Classic says: "It presides over Mount Huayin, Liang, Yong, and Yizhou, and also over the lodges Strider, Bond, Stomach, Hairy Head, Net, Beak, and Three Stars."
translations.idiomatic: The Star Classic states: "It governs Mount Huayin and the regions Liang, Yong, and Yizhou, and also the lodges Strider, Bond, Stomach, Hairy Head, Net, Beak, and Three Stars."

sentences.zh: 出西方，失行，外國敗。

translations.literal: Emerging in the west and losing its proper course: foreign states are defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When it rises in the west and strays from its path, neighboring states beyond the borders are broken.

sentences.zh: 出東方，失行，中國敗。

translations.literal: Emerging in the east and losing its proper course: the central state is defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When it rises in the east and strays from its path, the central realm is broken.

sentences.zh: 若經天，天下革，民更主，是謂亂紀，人衆流亡。

translations.literal: If it crosses the meridian, the realm is transformed, the people receive a new ruler; this is called disorder in the celestial order, and the multitudes flee as exiles.
translations.idiomatic: Should it cross the meridian, the empire is overturned and the people gain a new lord; this is termed chaos in the heavenly norm, and the masses scatter in flight.

sentences.zh: 晝見，與日爭明，強國弱，女主昌，又曰主大臣。

translations.literal: Visible by day, vying in brightness with the sun: strong states weaken, the chief consort flourishes; another account says it presides over great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: If seen in daylight, contending in brilliance with the sun, mighty states decline while the empress rises; another reading says it governs the fate of high ministers.

sentences.zh: 巫咸曰：光明見影，戰勝，歲熟。

translations.literal: Wu Xian says: when bright and casting a shadow, battles are won and the year is ripe.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xian writes: when Venus shines brightly enough to cast a shadow, armies triumph and the harvest is full.

sentences.zh: 狀炎然而上，兵起。

translations.literal: Blazing as it climbs upward: armies rise.
translations.idiomatic: If it burns like flame as it ascends, war breaks out.

sentences.zh: 光如張蓋，下有立王。

translations.literal: Light like an unfurled canopy: a king is established below.
translations.idiomatic: If its radiance spreads like an opened canopy, a new king is raised below.

sentences.zh: 凡與歲星相犯，兵敗失地。

translations.literal: Whenever it mutually transgresses Jupiter, armies are defeated and territory is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Venus and Jupiter mutually transgress, armies are broken and lands are lost.

sentences.zh: 犯熒惑，客敗主勝。

translations.literal: Transgressing Mars: the guest is defeated and the host prevails.
translations.idiomatic: If it transgresses Mars, the invader is beaten and the defender wins.

sentences.zh: 犯填星，太子不安，失地。

translations.literal: Transgressing Saturn: the crown prince is unsettled and territory is lost.
translations.idiomatic: If it transgresses Saturn, the heir apparent is disturbed and lands are forfeited.

sentences.zh: 犯辰星，主兵。

translations.literal: Transgressing Mercury: the ruler takes up arms.
translations.idiomatic: If it transgresses Mercury, the sovereign goes to war.

sentences.zh: 入月，主死，其下兵。

translations.literal: Entering the moon: the ruler dies, and armies march beneath.
translations.idiomatic: If it enters the moon, the sovereign dies and troops take the field below.

sentences.zh: 犯月角，兵起，在左則中國勝，在右則外國勝。

translations.literal: Transgressing the horn of the moon: war rises; if on the left the central state prevails, if on the right foreign states prevail.
translations.idiomatic: If it strikes the moon's horn, war begins; when the omen falls on the left the central realm wins, on the right the outer states win.

sentences.zh: 當見不見，失地破軍。

translations.literal: When it should appear but does not: territory is lost and armies are broken.
translations.idiomatic: If it ought to be visible yet fails to appear, lands are lost and hosts are shattered.

sentences.zh: 他星犯，其事急。

translations.literal: Other stars transgress: the matter is urgent.
translations.idiomatic: When other stars transgress Venus, the crisis is immediate.

sentences.zh: 祅星犯，邊城有戰。

translations.literal: A malefic star transgresses: border fortresses see battle.
translations.idiomatic: If a malefic star strikes it, frontier cities go to war.

sentences.zh: 客星犯，主兵將死。

translations.literal: A guest star transgresses: the ruler's armies and generals die.
translations.idiomatic: If a guest star transgresses it, the sovereign's soldiers and commanders perish.

sentences.zh: 凡太白至午位，避日而伏，若行至未，即爲經天，其災異重也。

translations.literal: Whenever Venus reaches the noon position, it hides from the sun; if it proceeds to wei, it crosses the meridian, and the calamity is grave indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Venus attains the noon quarter it hides before the sun; if it advances into wei it crosses the meridian, and the omen is exceedingly severe.

sentences.zh: 辰星爲北方，爲冬，爲水。

translations.literal: The Chronogram Star is the north, winter, and water.
translations.idiomatic: Mercury presides over the north, the season of winter, and the element of water.

sentences.zh: 于人五常，智也；

translations.literal: Among the five constant virtues in man, it is wisdom;
translations.idiomatic: In human affairs it corresponds to the virtue of wisdom;

sentences.zh: 五事，聽也。

translations.literal: among the five affairs, it is hearing.
translations.idiomatic: among the five governmental concerns, it governs the power of hearing.

sentences.zh: 常以二月春分見奎、婁，五月夏至見東井，八月秋分見角、亢，十一月冬至見牽牛。

translations.literal: Regularly at the spring equinox in the second month it appears at Strider and Bond; at the summer solstice in the fifth month at Well; at the autumn equinox in the eighth month at Horn and Neck; and at the winter solstice in the eleventh month at Ox Leader.
translations.idiomatic: It habitually appears at Strider and Bond at the spring equinox in the second month, at Well at the summer solstice in the fifth month, at Horn and Neck at the autumn equinox in the eighth month, and at Ox Leader at the winter solstice in the eleventh month.

sentences.zh: 出以辰戌，入以丑未，二旬而入。

translations.literal: It emerges at chen and xu, sets at chou and wei, and sets after twenty days.
translations.idiomatic: It rises at chen and xu, sets at chou and wei, and disappears after twenty days.

sentences.zh: 晨候之東方，夕候之西方也。

translations.literal: In the morning it is observed in the east; in the evening it is observed in the west.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn one watches for it in the east; at dusk one watches in the west.

sentences.zh: 一年一周天。

translations.literal: One year completes one circuit of heaven.
translations.idiomatic: It completes one revolution of the heavens in a year.

sentences.zh: 出早爲月食，晚爲彗星及天祅。

translations.literal: Emerging early: lunar eclipse; emerging late: comets and celestial portents.
translations.idiomatic: If it appears too early, a lunar eclipse follows; if too late, comets and heavenly anomalies appear.

sentences.zh: 一時不出，其時不和。

translations.literal: If it fails to appear in one season, that season falls out of harmony.
translations.idiomatic: When it misses one season, that season loses its proper balance.

sentences.zh: 四時不出，天下大饑。

translations.literal: If it fails to appear in all four seasons, the realm suffers great famine.
translations.idiomatic: When it fails to appear through all four seasons, famine ravages the empire.

sentences.zh: 《星經》曰：「主常山、冀、並、幽州，又主鬥、牛、女、虛、危、室、壁。」

translations.literal: The Star Classic says: "It presides over Mount Chang, Ji, Bing, and Youzhou, and also over the lodges Dipper, Ox, Girl, Void, Rooftop, Encampment, and Wall."
translations.idiomatic: The Star Classic states: "It governs Mount Chang and the regions Ji, Bing, and Youzhou, and also the lodges Dipper, Ox, Girl, Void, Rooftop, Encampment, and Wall."

sentences.zh: 又曰主燕、趙、代，主廷尉，以比宰相之象。

translations.literal: It also says it presides over Yan, Zhao, and Dai, and presides over the Minister of Justice, serving as the image of the chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: It further states that it governs Yan, Zhao, and Dai, rules the office of Minister of Justice, and stands as the emblem of the prime minister.

sentences.zh: 石申曰：色黃，五穀熟；

translations.literal: Shi Shen says: yellow color: the five grains ripen;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Shen writes: if yellow, the five grains mature;

sentences.zh: 黑，爲水；

translations.literal: black: floods;
translations.idiomatic: if black, there are inundations;

sentences.zh: 蒼白，爲喪。

translations.literal: dark white: mourning.
translations.idiomatic: if pale white, mourning follows.

sentences.zh: 凡與歲星相犯，皇后有謀。

translations.literal: Whenever it mutually transgresses Jupiter, the empress plots.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Mercury and Jupiter mutually transgress, the empress harbors designs.

sentences.zh: 熒惑犯，妨太子。

translations.literal: Mars transgresses: harm to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: If Mars transgresses Mercury, the heir apparent is harmed.

sentences.zh: 填星犯，兵敗；

translations.literal: Saturn transgresses: armies are defeated;
translations.idiomatic: If Saturn transgresses it, armies are broken;

sentences.zh: 太白亦然。

translations.literal: Venus likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Venus has the same effect.

sentences.zh: 芒角相及同光曰合，他星光曜相逮爲害。

translations.literal: When horned rays meet and their light merges it is called conjunction; when the radiance of other stars presses close, harm follows.
translations.idiomatic: If horned rays touch and shine together, the event is conjunction; when another star's light closes upon it, injury ensues.

sentences.zh: 客星、太陰、流星相犯，主內患。

translations.literal: Guest stars, the Great Yin, and meteors transgress: internal troubles arise.
translations.idiomatic: When guest stars, the moon, or meteors transgress Mercury, troubles stir within the realm.

sentences.zh: 凡五星：歲星色青，比參左肩；

translations.literal: Of the five stars in general: the Year Star is green, comparable to the left shoulder of Three Stars;
translations.idiomatic: As a rule among the five planets: Jupiter is green, matching the left shoulder of Three Stars;

sentences.zh: 熒惑色赤，比心大星；

translations.literal: the Sparkling Deluder is red, comparable to the great star of Heart;
translations.idiomatic: Mars is red, matching the great star of Heart;

sentences.zh: 填星色黃，比參右肩；

translations.literal: the Emplacement Star is yellow, comparable to the right shoulder of Three Stars;
translations.idiomatic: Saturn is yellow, matching the right shoulder of Three Stars;

sentences.zh: 太白色白，比狼星；

translations.literal: the Great White is white, comparable to the Wolf Star;
translations.idiomatic: Venus is white, matching the Wolf Star;

sentences.zh: 辰星色黑，比奎大星。

translations.literal: the Chronogram Star is black, comparable to the great star of Strider.
translations.idiomatic: Mercury is black, matching the great star of Strider.

sentences.zh: 得其常色而應四時則吉，變常爲凶。

translations.literal: When they display their proper colors and respond to the four seasons, the omen is auspicious; when they change from the norm, the omen is inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: If each keeps its proper hue and answers to the four seasons, fortune follows; if they depart from the norm, disaster follows.

sentences.zh: 木與土合爲內亂，饑；

translations.literal: Wood conjoining with earth: internal disorder and famine;
translations.idiomatic: When Jupiter conjoins with Saturn, civil strife and hunger arise;

sentences.zh: 與水合爲變謀而更事；

translations.literal: with water: plots shift and affairs are changed;
translations.idiomatic: with Mercury, schemes are altered and affairs are overturned;

sentences.zh: 與火合爲饑，爲旱；

translations.literal: with fire: famine and drought;
translations.idiomatic: with Mars, famine and drought follow;

sentences.zh: 與金合爲白衣之會，合鬥，國有內亂，野有破軍，爲水。

translations.literal: with metal: an assembly in white robes; if they join in combat, internal disorder within the state, a broken army in the wild, and floods.
translations.idiomatic: with Venus, a gathering in mourning dress; if they fight, rebellion within the realm, a shattered host abroad, and inundation.

sentences.zh: 太白在南，歲星在北，名曰牝牡，年穀大熟。

translations.literal: Venus in the south and Jupiter in the north: this is called male and female, and the year's grain is greatly abundant.
translations.idiomatic: When Venus stands south and Jupiter north, the configuration is called male and female, and the harvest is exceedingly rich.

sentences.zh: 太白在北，歲星在南，其年或有或無。

translations.literal: Venus in the north and Jupiter in the south: that year's harvest may come or may fail.
translations.idiomatic: When Venus stands north and Jupiter south, the harvest of that year may appear or may not.

sentences.zh: 火與金合爲爍，爲喪，不可舉事用兵，從軍爲軍憂；

translations.literal: Fire conjoining with metal: blazing and mourning; one must not undertake affairs or raise armies; those who follow the army suffer military calamity;
translations.idiomatic: When Mars conjoins Venus, there is scorching heat and bereavement; affairs must not be launched nor armies raised, and those who join the host meet military disaster;

sentences.zh: 離之，軍卻。

translations.literal: when they separate, the army withdraws.
translations.idiomatic: when the two part, the army retreats.

sentences.zh: 出太白陰，分地；

translations.literal: Emerging from the yin side of Venus: territory is divided;
translations.idiomatic: If Mars emerges from the yin side of Venus, lands are partitioned;

sentences.zh: 出其陽，偏將戰。

translations.literal: emerging from its yang side: lieutenant generals do battle.
translations.idiomatic: if from the yang side, deputy commanders go to war.

sentences.zh: 與土合爲憂，主孽卿。

translations.literal: Conjoining with earth: sorrow, and the ruler's line is afflicted among the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When Mars conjoins Saturn, grief arises and the royal house suffers among its ministers.

sentences.zh: 與水合爲北軍，用兵舉事大敗。

translations.literal: Conjoining with water: the Northern Army; raising armies and undertaking affairs ends in great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When Mars conjoins Mercury, the Northern Army is signified; to mobilize troops or launch enterprises ends in utter defeat.

sentences.zh: 一曰，火與水合爲焠，不可舉事用兵。

translations.literal: One account says: fire conjoining with water is quenching, and one must not undertake affairs or raise armies.
translations.idiomatic: One tradition holds that Mars with Mercury is quenching, and affairs and armies must not be undertaken.

sentences.zh: 土與水合爲壅沮，不可舉事用兵，有覆軍。

translations.literal: Earth conjoining with water: obstruction and stagnation; one must not undertake affairs or raise armies, and armies are overthrown.
translations.idiomatic: When Saturn conjoins Mercury, blockage and stagnation follow; armies must not be raised nor enterprises begun, and hosts are overturned.

sentences.zh: 一曰，爲變謀更事，必爲旱。

translations.literal: One account says: plots shift and affairs change, and drought is certain to follow.
translations.idiomatic: One tradition says schemes are overturned and affairs are changed, and drought is sure to come.

sentences.zh: 與金合爲疾，爲白衣會，爲內兵，國亡地。

translations.literal: Conjoining with metal: disease, an assembly in white robes, internal warfare, and the state loses its territory.
translations.idiomatic: When Saturn conjoins Venus, pestilence follows, mourners assemble, civil war breaks out, and the state forfeits its lands.

sentences.zh: 與木合國饑。

translations.literal: Conjoining with wood: the state suffers famine.
translations.idiomatic: When Saturn conjoins Jupiter, the realm goes hungry.

sentences.zh: 水與金合爲變謀，爲兵、憂。

translations.literal: Water conjoining with metal: plots shift, and there is war and sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: When Mercury conjoins Venus, designs are altered, and war and grief follow.

sentences.zh: 木、火、土、金與水鬥，皆爲戰，兵不在外，皆爲內亂。

translations.literal: Wood, fire, earth, and metal all combating with water signify war; if armies are not abroad, all signify internal disorder.
translations.idiomatic: When Jupiter, Mars, Saturn, and Venus all fight Mercury, the omen is war; if no armies stand abroad, the omen is rebellion within.

sentences.zh: 三星合，是謂驚立絕行，其國外內有兵與喪，百姓饑乏，改立侯王。
