translations.literal: Three stars conjoining: this is called startled standing and halted movement; within and without the state there are armies and mourning, the people hunger and are destitute, and marquis-kings are replaced.
translations.idiomatic: When three planets conjoin, the omen is called startled standing and arrested motion: armies and mourning arise at home and abroad, the people starve and are exhausted, and feudal lords are set aside.

sentences.zh: 四星合，是謂大湯，其國兵、喪並起，君子憂，小人流。

translations.literal: Four stars conjoining: this is called great convulsion; the state knows armies and mourning together, gentlemen are troubled, and petty men run rampant.
translations.idiomatic: When four planets conjoin, the omen is called great upheaval: war and mourning rise together, the worthy are anxious, and base men flourish.

sentences.zh: 五星若合，是謂易行，有德，受慶，改立王者，奄有四方，子孫蕃昌；

translations.literal: If the five stars conjoin, this is called altered motion; if there is virtue, blessing is received, kings are replaced, and the realm is possessed in all four quarters with descendants multiplying;
translations.idiomatic: If all five planets conjoin, the omen is called changed course: where virtue reigns, grace is granted, a new king is raised, the four quarters are seized, and posterity flourishes;

sentences.zh: 亡德受殃，離其國家，滅其宗廟，百姓離去，被滿四方。

translations.literal: without virtue calamity is received, one is driven from the state, ancestral temples are destroyed, the people depart, and suffering spreads to fill the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: where virtue fails, disaster falls, the dynasty is cast out, the ancestral shrines are ruined, the people flee, and affliction floods every direction.

sentences.zh: 五星皆大，其事亦大；

translations.literal: When all five stars are large, the event is great;
translations.idiomatic: When every planet appears large, the event is momentous;

sentences.zh: 皆小，事亦小。

translations.literal: when all are small, the event is small.
translations.idiomatic: when all appear small, the event is slight.

sentences.zh: 五星俱見，其年必惡。

translations.literal: When all five stars are visible together, that year is sure to be ill-omened.
translations.idiomatic: If all five appear at once, that year is bound to be disastrous.

sentences.zh: 凡五星與列宿相去方寸爲犯，居之不去爲守，兩體俱動而直曰觸，離復合、合復離曰鬥，當東反西曰退，芒角相及同舍曰合。

translations.literal: Of the five stars in general, separation from a fixed star by a cun or so is called transgression; dwelling there without departing is called stationing; both bodies moving and meeting straight on is called striking; separating and rejoining or joining and separating again is called combat; turning west when it should move east is called retrograde; horned rays meeting and sharing a lodge is called conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: As a rule for the five planets: standing a few minutes of arc from a lodge star is transgression; remaining without leaving is stationing; both bodies in motion meeting head-on is striking; parting and reuniting, or uniting and parting again, is combat; moving west instead of east is retrograde; horned rays touching within the same lodge is conjunction.

sentences.zh: 凡五星東行爲順，西行曰逆，順則疾，逆則遲，通而率之，終於東行。

translations.literal: Of the five stars in general, eastward motion is called direct, westward motion is called retrograde; direct motion is swift, retrograde motion is slow; taken together and averaged, they end by moving eastward.
translations.idiomatic: As a rule for the five planets: motion to the east is direct, to the west retrograde; direct motion is fast, retrograde slow; measured overall and reduced to a mean rate, they finish by advancing eastward.

sentences.zh: 不東不西曰留，與日相近而不見曰伏，伏與日同度曰合。

translations.literal: Neither east nor west is called lingering; drawing near the sun and becoming invisible is called hiding; hiding at the same degree as the sun is called conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: Motion neither east nor west is lingering; drawing close to the sun and vanishing from sight is hiding; hiding at the sun's degree is conjunction.

sentences.zh: 凡金、水二星，行速而不經天，自始與日合後，行速而先日，夕見西方。

translations.literal: Of metal and water, the two stars move swiftly and do not cross the meridian; from their first conjunction with the sun they move quickly ahead of the sun and are seen at evening in the west.
translations.idiomatic: Venus and Mercury, the two swift planets, do not cross the meridian; from their initial conjunction with the sun they race ahead of it and appear in the western sky at dusk.

sentences.zh: 去日前稍遠，夕時欲近南方則漸遲，遲極則留，留而近日，則逆行而合日；

translations.literal: As they draw slightly farther from the sun, and at evening approach the south, they gradually slow; at the limit of slowness they linger, and lingering while nearing the sun, they retrograde and conjoin with the sun;
translations.idiomatic: As they pull somewhat away from the sun and at evening draw toward the south, they gradually slow; at maximum slowness they linger, and while lingering near the sun they turn retrograde and unite with it;

sentences.zh: 在於日後，晨見東方。

translations.literal: being behind the sun, they are seen at dawn in the east.
translations.idiomatic: then, lying behind the sun, they appear in the eastern sky at morning.

sentences.zh: 逆極則留，留而後遲，遲極去日稍遠，旦時欲近南方，則遠行以追日，晨伏於東方，復與日合度。

translations.literal: At the limit of retrograde they linger; after lingering they again slow; at the limit of slowness, as they draw somewhat farther from the sun and at dawn approach the south, they move swiftly to pursue the sun, hide at dawn in the east, and again conjoin in degree with the sun.
translations.idiomatic: At the limit of retrograde they linger; after lingering they slow once more; at maximum slowness, as they stand somewhat farther from the sun and at dawn draw toward the south, they hurry forward to chase the sun, vanish in the eastern dawn, and again conjoin with the sun in degree.

sentences.zh: 此五星合見、遲疾、順逆、留行之大端也。

translations.literal: These are the great outlines of the five planets' conjunction, slowness and swiftness, direct and retrograde motion, lingering, and visibility.
translations.idiomatic: These are the principal patterns of the five planets in conjunction, in swift and slow motion, in direct and retrograde course, in lingering, and in appearing and hiding.

sentences.zh: 凡五星之行，古法：周天之數，如歲星謂十二年一周天，乃約數耳。

translations.literal: Of the motion of the five stars, the ancient method counted circuits of heaven: saying, for example, that the Year Star completes one circuit in twelve years is only a rough number.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient reckoning of the five planets' motion, the circuits of heaven were rounded figures: to say, for instance, that Jupiter completes one revolution in twelve years is merely an approximation.

sentences.zh: 晉灼謂太歲在四仲則行三宿，在四孟、四季則行二宿，故十二年而行周二十八宿。

translations.literal: Jin Zhuo held that when the Grand Year stands in one of the four mid-season months it advances three lodges, and in the four first or last months of the seasons two lodges, thus completing the twenty-eight lodges in twelve years.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhuo argued that when the Grand Year occupies one of the four central months it moves three lodges, and in the four initial or final months of the seasons two lodges, thereby traversing the twenty-eight lodges in twelve years.

sentences.zh: 其說亦非。

translations.literal: That explanation also is not correct.
translations.idiomatic: That account, too, is mistaken.

sentences.zh: 夫二十八宿，度有廣狹，而歲星之行自有盈縮，豈得以十二年一周無差忒乎？

translations.literal: The twenty-eight lodges vary in breadth and narrowness, while the Year Star's motion has its own expansions and contractions—how could twelve years complete one circuit without discrepancy?
translations.idiomatic: The twenty-eight lodges are unequal in width, and Jupiter's course has its own swelling and shrinking—how could one revolution in exactly twelve years pass without error?

sentences.zh: 唐一行始言歲星自商、周迄春秋季年，率百二十餘年而超一次，因以爲常。

translations.literal: Tang Yixing first said that from the Shang and Zhou through the Spring and Autumn, in alternate years on average, a little more than 120 years were required for one overshoot, and he took this as constant.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Yixing first proposed that from the Shang and Zhou down through the Spring and Autumn period, Jupiter on average required a little over 120 years to leap one lodge ahead, and he treated this as a fixed rule.

sentences.zh: 以春秋亂世則其行速，時平則其行遲，其說尤迂。

translations.literal: He also said that in ages of disorder its motion is swift and in ages of peace it is slow—the explanation is especially strained.
translations.idiomatic: He further held that in chaotic times the planet moves quickly and in tranquil times slowly—a doctrine still more forced.

sentences.zh: 既乃爲後率前率之術以求之，則其說自悖矣。

translations.literal: Then he devised a method of deriving later rates from earlier rates to seek the result, and his own account contradicts itself.
translations.idiomatic: He then devised a procedure of deriving later ratios from earlier ratios to obtain the answer, and in doing so his theory refutes itself.

sentences.zh: 今紹興曆法，歲星每年行一百四十五分，是每年行一次之外有餘一分，積一百四十四年剩一次矣。

translations.literal: In the calendar of the Shaoxing reign, the Year Star advances 145 parts each year, so that beyond one lodge per year there remains one part; accumulated over 144 years this amounts to one extra lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Shaoxing calendar, Jupiter advances 145 parts each year, leaving one part beyond a full lodge annually; accumulated over 144 years this yields one lodge in surplus.

sentences.zh: 然則先儒之說安可信乎？

translations.literal: In that case, how can the explanations of earlier scholars be trusted?
translations.idiomatic: If so, how can the doctrines of the former masters be relied upon?

sentences.zh: 餘四星之行，固無逆順，中間亦豈無差忒？

translations.literal: The motion of the other four stars indeed has no retrograde or direct distinction in the same way, yet how could there be no discrepancies in between?
translations.idiomatic: The courses of the other four planets, it is true, do not show the same alternation of retrograde and direct motion, yet how could no errors arise in their intervals?

sentences.zh: 一行不復詳言，蓋亦知之矣。

translations.literal: Yixing did not explain this in detail, probably because he knew it himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yixing did not treat the matter exhaustively, likely because he understood the difficulty already.

sentences.zh: 景星，德星也，一曰瑞星，如半月，生於晦朔，大而中空，其名各異。

translations.literal: The Luminous Star is the star of virtue, also called the auspicious star; shaped like a half moon, born at new and full moon, large and hollow within, its names differ.
translations.idiomatic: The Luminous Star is a star of virtue, also termed an auspicious star; it resembles a half moon, appears at new and full moon, is great and hollow within, and bears many names.

sentences.zh: 曰周伯，其色黃，煌煌然，所見之國大昌。

translations.literal: Called Zhou Bo, its color is yellow and blazing bright; the state where it appears flourishes greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Named Zhou Bo, it shines yellow and resplendent; the country beneath its appearance prospers mightily.

sentences.zh: 曰含譽，光耀似彗，喜則含譽射。

translations.literal: Called Han Yu, its radiance resembles a comet; when there is joy, Han Yu shoots forth.
translations.idiomatic: Named Han Yu, its light is comet-like; in times of rejoicing Han Yu flares outward.

sentences.zh: 曰格澤，狀如炎火，下大上銳，色黃白，起地上，見則不種而獲。

translations.literal: Called Ge Ze, shaped like blazing fire, broad below and sharp above, yellow-white in color, rising from the ground; when seen, crops are harvested without sowing.
translations.idiomatic: Named Ge Ze, it looks like burning flame, wide below and pointed above, yellow-white, rising from the earth; when it appears, grain is gathered though none was planted.

sentences.zh: 曰歸邪，兩赤彗向上，有蓋。

translations.literal: Called Gui Xie, two red comets point upward with a canopy above.
translations.idiomatic: Named Gui Xie, two red comets rise upward beneath a covering canopy.

sentences.zh: 曰天保星，有音，如炬火下地、野雞鳴。

translations.literal: Called Tianbao, it has sound, like a torch falling to earth and a wild cock crowing.
translations.idiomatic: Named Tianbao, it gives forth sound, like a torch plunging to the ground and a pheasant calling in the wild.

sentences.zh: 皆五行沖和之氣所生也。

translations.literal: All are born of the harmonious qi of the five phases.
translations.idiomatic: All are engendered by the balanced breath of the five agents.

sentences.zh: 其王蓬芮、玄保、昭明、昏昌、旬始、司危、菟昌、地維臧光之類，亦皆爲瑞星。

translations.literal: Wang Pengrui, Xuanbao, Zhaoming, Hunchang, Xunshi, Siwei, Tuchang, Diwei Zangguang, and the like are also all auspicious stars.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pengrui, Xuanbao, Zhaoming, Hunchang, Xunshi, Siwei, Tuchang, Diwei Zangguang, and their kind are likewise counted as auspicious stars.

sentences.zh: 然前志以王蓬芮已下星爲妖星。

translations.literal: Yet the previous monograph classifies Wang Pengrui and the stars below it as malefic stars.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the earlier treatise ranks Wang Pengrui and the stars following it among malefic stars.

sentences.zh: 又奇星，古無所考，見於仁宗、英宗之時，故附于景星之末云。

translations.literal: As for the strange stars, antiquity offers no investigation; they appear in the reigns of Renzong and Yingzong, and so are appended at the end of the section on Luminous Stars.
translations.idiomatic: The odd stars cannot be verified in antiquity; they were observed in the reigns of Renzong and Yingzong, and are therefore appended at the close of the Luminous Star account.

sentences.zh: 彗星，小者數寸，長者或竟天。

translations.literal: Comets: the small measure a few inches, the long may span the whole sky.
translations.idiomatic: Comets may be only a few inches across, or their tails may stretch across the entire heavens.

sentences.zh: 見則兵起，大水，除舊佈新之兆也。

translations.literal: When they appear, armies rise, great floods come, and they are omens of removing the old and spreading the new.
translations.idiomatic: When they appear, war breaks out and great floods follow; they portend the clearing away of the old and the laying out of the new.

sentences.zh: 其體無光，傅日而爲光。

translations.literal: Their bodies have no light of their own but borrow the sun to shine.
translations.idiomatic: They possess no light of their own but take the sun's light to become luminous.

sentences.zh: 故夕見則東指，晨見則西指。

translations.literal: Thus seen at evening they point east; seen at dawn they point west.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore when seen at dusk they point eastward; when seen at dawn they point westward.

sentences.zh: 光芒所及則爲災。

translations.literal: Wherever their radiance reaches, disaster follows.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever their light falls, calamity ensues.

sentences.zh: 有五色，各依五行本精所生。

translations.literal: They have five colors, each born of the root essence of its phase among the five agents.
translations.idiomatic: They display five colors, each produced from the fundamental essence of its corresponding agent.

sentences.zh: 孛星，彗屬。

translations.literal: The Broom Star belongs to the comet class.
translations.idiomatic: The Broom Star belongs to the comet family.

sentences.zh: 偏指曰彗，芒氣四出曰孛。

translations.literal: Pointing to one side is called a comet; qi with rays shooting out on four sides is called a broom.
translations.idiomatic: A body pointing in one direction is called a comet; a haze with rays bursting forth on four sides is called a broom star.

sentences.zh: 孛者，孛孛然，非常惡氣之所生也。

translations.literal: A broom is broom-like; it is born of exceedingly malign qi.
translations.idiomatic: A broom star spreads like a broom; it arises from profoundly inauspicious vapor.

sentences.zh: 主大亂，主大兵，災甚於彗。

translations.literal: It presides over great disorder and great war; its calamity exceeds that of a comet.
translations.idiomatic: It governs great rebellion and great warfare, and its disaster is worse than that of an ordinary comet.

sentences.zh: 旄頭星，《玉冊》云：亦彗屬也。

translations.literal: The Banner Head Star: the Jade Register says it also belongs to the comet class.
translations.idiomatic: The Banner Head Star: the Jade Register states that it, too, belongs to the comet family.

sentences.zh: 客星有五：周伯、老子、王蓬絮、國皇、溫星是也。

translations.literal: Guest stars are five in kind: Zhou Bo, Laozi, Wang Pengxu, Guohuang, and Wen Star.
translations.idiomatic: There are five kinds of guest stars: Zhou Bo, Laozi, Wang Pengxu, Guohuang, and Wen Star.

sentences.zh: 周伯，大而黃，煌煌然，所見之國，兵喪，饑饉，民庶流亡。

translations.literal: Zhou Bo is large and yellow, blazing bright; the state where it appears suffers war and mourning, famine, and the people flee as exiles.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Bo is great and yellow, shining brilliantly; the country beneath it knows war and bereavement, hunger, and a people driven into exile.

sentences.zh: 老子，明大純白，出則爲饑，爲凶，爲善，爲惡，爲喜，爲怒。

translations.literal: Laozi is bright, great, pure white; when it appears there is famine, disaster, good, evil, joy, and anger.
translations.idiomatic: Laozi shines bright, large, and pure white; when it appears there is hunger and misfortune, good and ill, joy and wrath.

sentences.zh: 王蓬絮，狀如粉絮，拂拂然，見則其國兵起，有白衣之會。

translations.literal: Wang Pengxu is shaped like powdered floss, fluttering; when seen, that state raises armies and there is an assembly in white robes.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pengxu looks like powdered cotton, drifting and trembling; when it appears, that country mobilizes troops and mourners gather in white.

sentences.zh: 國皇，大而黃白，有芒角，主兵起，水災，人主惡之。

translations.literal: Guohuang is large, yellow-white, with horned rays; it presides over armies rising, flood disaster, and the ruler's hatred of it.
translations.idiomatic: Guohuang is great, yellow-white, and horned; it governs the rise of armies, inundation, and the sovereign's dread of the omen.

sentences.zh: 溫星，色白，狀如風動搖，常出四隅。

translations.literal: Wen Star is white in color, shaped like wind shaking; it regularly appears in the four corners.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Star is white, shaped as if wind were swaying it, and commonly appears in the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 皆主兵。

translations.literal: All preside over war.
translations.idiomatic: All signify warfare.

sentences.zh: 此五星錯出乎五緯之間，其見無期，其行無度，各以其所在分野而占之。

translations.literal: These five stars appear irregularly among the five planets; their appearances have no fixed season, their motion no fixed measure, and each is interpreted according to the territorial division where it stands.
translations.idiomatic: These five stars emerge unpredictably among the five planets; they appear without fixed season and move without fixed pace, and each is read according to the regional domain beneath it.

sentences.zh: 又四隅各有三星：東南曰盜星，主大盜；

translations.literal: In each of the four corners there are also three stars: in the southeast, the Robber Star, presiding over great robbery;
translations.idiomatic: In each of the four directions there are also three stars: in the southeast, the Robber Star, governing great theft;

sentences.zh: 西南曰種陵，出則穀貴；

translations.literal: in the southwest, Zhongling; when it appears grain is dear;
translations.idiomatic: in the southwest, Zhongling; when it appears grain becomes costly;

sentences.zh: 西北曰天狗，見則天下大饑；

translations.literal: in the northwest, the Celestial Dog; when seen, the realm suffers great famine;
translations.idiomatic: in the northwest, the Celestial Dog; when seen, famine ravages the empire;

sentences.zh: 東北曰女帛，主有大喪。

translations.literal: in the northeast, Nübo, presiding over great mourning.
translations.idiomatic: in the northeast, Nübo, governing great bereavement.

sentences.zh: 流星，天使也。

translations.literal: Meteors are heavenly envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Meteors are emissaries of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 自上而降曰流，東西橫行亦曰流。

translations.literal: Descending from above is called streaming; moving east or west across the sky is also called streaming.
translations.idiomatic: Falling from on high is called streaming; crossing east or west is also called streaming.

sentences.zh: 流星有八，曰天使，曰天暉，曰天雁，曰天保，曰地雁，曰梁星，曰營頭，曰天狗。

translations.literal: Meteors are eight in kind: Heavenly Envoy, Heavenly Splendor, Heavenly Wild Goose, Tianbao, Earth Wild Goose, Beam Star, Banner Head, and Celestial Dog.
translations.idiomatic: There are eight kinds of meteors: Heavenly Envoy, Heavenly Splendor, Heavenly Wild Goose, Tianbao, Earth Wild Goose, Beam Star, Banner Head, and Celestial Dog.

sentences.zh: 流星之爲天使者，有祥有妖，爲天暉、天雁、夜隕而爲天保，則祥；

translations.literal: Of meteors that serve as heavenly envoys, some are auspicious and some malign: if at night they fall as Heavenly Splendor or Heavenly Wild Goose, or fall at night and become Tianbao, the omen is auspicious;
translations.idiomatic: Among meteors acting as heavenly envoys, some bring fortune and some disaster: if by night they fall as Heavenly Splendor or Heavenly Wild Goose, or fall at night and become Tianbao, the sign is lucky;

sentences.zh: 若夜隕而爲地雁、梁星，晝隕而爲營頭，則妖。

translations.literal: if by night they fall as Earth Wild Goose or Beam Star, or by day fall as Banner Head, the omen is malign.
translations.idiomatic: if by night they fall as Earth Wild Goose or Beam Star, or by day fall as Banner Head, the sign is unlucky.

sentences.zh: 流星之大者爲奔星，夜隕而爲天狗，厥妖大。

translations.literal: The largest meteors are called rushing stars; if they fall at night and become the Celestial Dog, the malign omen is great.
translations.idiomatic: The greatest meteors are called rushing stars; if they fall at night and become the Celestial Dog, the disaster is severe.

sentences.zh: 自下而升曰飛。

translations.literal: Rising from below upward is called flying.
translations.idiomatic: Ascending from below is called flying.

sentences.zh: 飛星有五，亦有妖祥之分，飛星化而爲天刑則祥；

translations.literal: Flying stars are five in kind, also divided into malign and auspicious; if a flying star transforms into Celestial Punishment, the omen is auspicious;
translations.idiomatic: There are five kinds of flying stars, likewise divided into fortune and disaster: if a flying star changes into Celestial Punishment, the sign is lucky;

sentences.zh: 爲降石，爲頓頑，爲解銜，爲大滑，則爲妖。

translations.literal: if it becomes Falling Stone, Dunwan, Jie Xian, or Great Slip, the omen is malign.
translations.idiomatic: if it becomes Falling Stone, Dunwan, Jie Xian, or Great Slip, the sign is unlucky.

sentences.zh: 妖星，五行乖戾之氣也。

translations.literal: Malefic stars are the qi of perverse imbalance among the five phases.
translations.idiomatic: Malefic stars are the breath of discord among the five agents.

sentences.zh: 五星之精，散而爲妖星，形狀不同，爲殃則一。

translations.literal: The essences of the five planets scatter and become malefic stars; their shapes differ, yet the harm they bring is one.
translations.idiomatic: The refined essences of the five planets disperse into malefic stars; though their forms vary, the calamity they work is the same.

sentences.zh: 各以其所見日期、分野、形色，占爲兵、饑、水、旱、亂、亡。

translations.literal: According to the date of appearance, territorial division, and form and color, they are interpreted as war, famine, flood, drought, disorder, or ruin.
translations.idiomatic: By the day they appear, the region beneath them, and their shape and hue, they are read as portents of war, hunger, water, drought, rebellion, or destruction.

sentences.zh: 星長三尺至五尺，期百日，等而上之，至一丈期一年，三丈期三年，五丈期五年，十丈期七年，十丈已上，不出九年。

translations.literal: A star three to five chi in length: its term is one hundred days; by equal steps upward, one zhang is one year, three zhang three years, five zhang five years, ten zhang seven years; above ten zhang, the term does not exceed nine years.
translations.idiomatic: A star three to five feet long runs a course of one hundred days; by equal increments, one zhang means one year, three zhang three years, five zhang five years, ten zhang seven years; beyond ten zhang the term does not pass nine years.

sentences.zh: 蓋妖星長大則期遠而殃深，短小則期近而殃淺。

translations.literal: In general, when a malefic star is long and large its term is distant and its harm deep; when short and small its term is near and its harm shallow.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly speaking, a large, long malefic star portends a distant term and deep disaster; a short, small one a near term and lighter harm.

sentences.zh: 天攙星乃歲之精，主奮爭。

translations.literal: The Celestial Interference Star is the essence of the Year Star and presides over fierce struggle.
translations.idiomatic: The Celestial Interference Star is Jupiter's essence and governs violent contention.

sentences.zh: 天槍如彗，出西方，長二三尺，名天槍，主破國。

translations.literal: The Celestial Spear is comet-like, appearing in the west two or three chi long; named the Celestial Spear, it presides over the breaking of states.
translations.idiomatic: The Celestial Spear resembles a comet, emerging in the west two or three feet long; called the Celestial Spear, it governs the ruin of kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 天猾主招亂。

translations.literal: The Celestial Mischief presides over summoning disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The Celestial Mischief governs the incitement of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 天棓出西方，長數丈，主國亂。

translations.literal: The Celestial Club emerges in the west several zhang long and presides over national disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The Celestial Club appears in the west several zhang in length and governs turmoil within the realm.

sentences.zh: 蚩尤旗類彗而後曲，主兵。

translations.literal: The Banner of Chiyou is comet-like but curves backward and presides over war.
translations.idiomatic: The Banner of Chiyou resembles a comet yet bends backward, and governs warfare.

sentences.zh: 天沖狀如人，蒼衣赤首，不動，主下謀上，滅國。

translations.literal: The Celestial Assault is shaped like a man in dark robes with a red head; motionless, it presides over subordinates plotting against superiors and the destruction of states.
translations.idiomatic: The Celestial Assault looks like a man in dark garments with a red head; if it does not move, it governs plots by inferiors against superiors and the fall of kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 國皇大而赤，去地三丈，如炬火，主內寇。

translations.literal: Guohuang is large and red, three zhang from the ground, like a torch flame, and presides over internal enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Guohuang is great and red, three zhang above the earth, like a blazing torch, and governs foes within the realm.

sentences.zh: 及登主夷分，主恣虐，旦見則主弱。

translations.literal: Jideng presides over the partition of the ruler's domain; it presides over wanton cruelty, and if seen at dawn the ruler is weakened.
translations.idiomatic: Jideng governs the splitting of the sovereign's lands; it governs cruel excess, and if seen at dawn the ruler grows feeble.

sentences.zh: 昭明如太白，光芒不行，主兵、喪。

translations.literal: Zhaoming is like the Great White, its radiance unmoving, and presides over war and mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoming resembles Venus, its light steady and untraveling, and governs war and bereavement.

sentences.zh: 司危，《天官書》如太白，有目，去地可六丈，大而白，其下有兵，主擊強。

translations.literal: Siwei: the Treatise on the Celestial Offices says it is like the Great White, with an eye, six zhang from the ground, large and white; below it are armies, and it presides over striking the strong.
translations.idiomatic: Siwei: the Treatise on the Celestial Offices describes it as like Venus, with an eye, about six zhang above the earth, great and white; armies lie beneath it, and it governs attacks upon the mighty.

sentences.zh: 五殘如辰星，去地六七丈，其下有兵，主奔亡。

translations.literal: Wucan is like the Chronogram Star, six or seven zhang from the ground; below it are armies, and it presides over flight and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Wucan resembles Mercury, six or seven zhang above the earth; armies lie beneath it, and it governs rout and destruction.

sentences.zh: 六賊去地六丈，大而赤，有光，出非其方，下有兵、喪。

translations.literal: Liuzzei is six zhang from the ground, large and red, with light; if it appears outside its proper quarter, below it are armies and mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Liuzzei stands six zhang above the earth, great and red and luminous; if it emerges outside its proper direction, armies and bereavement follow below.

sentences.zh: 獄漢青中赤表，下有三彗，去地可六丈，大而赤，數動。

translations.literal: Yuhan is green within and red without, with three comets below, about six zhang from the ground, large and red, moving repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Yuhan is green at the center and red at the surface, with three comets beneath, about six zhang above the earth, great and red, and quivering in motion.

sentences.zh: 大賁主滅邪暴兵。

translations.literal: Daben presides over extinguishing wickedness and violent armies.
translations.idiomatic: Daben governs the suppression of evil and brutal hosts.

sentences.zh: 燭星主滅邪。

translations.literal: Zhuxing presides over the extinction of evil.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuxing governs the quelling of wickedness.

sentences.zh: 絀流主伏逃。

translations.literal: Chuoliu presides over concealment and flight.
translations.idiomatic: Chuoliu governs hiding and escape.

sentences.zh: 茀星、昴、孛星主災。

translations.literal: Fei Star, Mao, and the Broom Star preside over disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Star, Mao, and the Broom Star govern calamity.

sentences.zh: 旬始出北斗旁，如雄雞，見則更主。

translations.literal: Xunshi appears beside the Dipper, shaped like a cock; when seen, the ruler is replaced.
translations.idiomatic: Xunshi emerges near the Dipper, shaped like a rooster; when it appears, the sovereign is changed.

sentences.zh: 擊咎主大兵，有反者，大亂。

translations.literal: Jijiu presides over great armies; if there are rebels, great disorder follows.
translations.idiomatic: Jijiu governs vast armies; if rebels arise, rebellion becomes general.

sentences.zh: 天杵主䍧羊。

translations.literal: The Celestial Pestle presides over rams.
translations.idiomatic: The Celestial Pestle governs sheep.

sentences.zh: 天柎主擊殃。

translations.literal: The Celestial Shaft presides over striking calamity.
translations.idiomatic: The Celestial Shaft governs the infliction of disaster.

sentences.zh: 伏靈見則世亂。

translations.literal: When Hidden Spirit appears, the age falls into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: When Hidden Spirit appears, the world is thrown into chaos.

sentences.zh: 天敗主鬥沖。

translations.literal: Celestial Defeat presides over violent collision.
translations.idiomatic: Celestial Defeat governs fierce clash and assault.

sentences.zh: 司奸主見怪。

translations.literal: Si Jian presides over the appearance of strangeness.
translations.idiomatic: Si Jian governs the manifestation of the uncanny.

sentences.zh: 天狗有毛，旁有短彗，下如狗形，見則兵饑。

translations.literal: The Celestial Dog has hair, with a short comet at its side, shaped like a dog below; when seen, armies hunger.
translations.idiomatic: The Celestial Dog is hairy, with a short comet at its side and the form of a dog below; when it appears, armies starve.

sentences.zh: 天殘主貪殘。

translations.literal: Celestial Ruin presides over greedy cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Celestial Ruin governs rapacity and brutality.

sentences.zh: 卒起有謀反，主驚亡。

translations.literal: Sudden Rise: if rebellion is plotted, the ruler is startled and perishes.
translations.idiomatic: Sudden Rise: if treason is plotted, the sovereign is alarmed and destroyed.

sentences.zh: 枉矢色黑，蛇行，望之如有毛目，長數匹者，見則兵起，破女君臣憂，上下亂。

translations.literal: Warped Arrow is black in color, moving like a serpent; viewed from afar it seems to have hair and eyes several pi in length; when seen, armies rise, the state is broken, ruler and ministers are troubled, and high and low fall into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Warped Arrow is black, writhing like a snake; seen from a distance it appears to have hair and eyes several tens of feet long; when it appears, war begins, the realm is shattered, sovereign and ministers are anguished, and order collapses above and below.

sentences.zh: 拂樞主制時。

translations.literal: Fushu presides over controlling the seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Fushu governs mastery over the seasons.

sentences.zh: 滅寶主伐亂。

translations.literal: Miebao presides over punitive campaigns against disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Miebao governs campaigns to suppress rebellion.

sentences.zh: 繞綎主亂孳。

translations.literal: Raogeng presides over chaotic proliferation.
translations.idiomatic: Raogeng governs riotous increase and disorderly growth.

sentences.zh: 驚理主相屠。

translations.literal: Jingli presides over mutual slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: Jingli governs mutual butchery.

sentences.zh: 大奮祀主招邪。

translations.literal: Dafensi presides over summoning evil.
translations.idiomatic: Dafensi governs the calling forth of malign forces.

sentences.zh: 天鋒彗象，形似矛鋒，見則兵起，有亂臣。

translations.literal: The Celestial Spear-Comet resembles the edge of a spear; when seen, armies rise and there are rebellious ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Celestial Spear-Comet is shaped like a spear point; when it appears, war breaks out and treacherous ministers arise.

sentences.zh: 昭星有三彗，兵出，有大盜不成，又主滅邪。

translations.literal: Zhaoxing has three comets; armies march forth, great robbers fail to succeed, and it also presides over the extinction of evil.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoxing bears three comets; troops take the field, great bandits do not prevail, and it also governs the quelling of wickedness.

sentences.zh: 蓬星大如二斗器，色白，出東南方，東北主旱，或大水。

translations.literal: Peng Star is as large as two dou vessels, white in color, appearing in the southeast; in the northeast it presides over drought, or great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Star is as great as two dou measures, white, appearing in the southeast; in the northeast it governs drought or great inundation.

sentences.zh: 長庚星如一匹布著天，見則兵起。

translations.literal: Chang Geng Star is like a bolt of cloth spread upon the sky; when seen, armies rise.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Geng Star is like a length of cloth draped across heaven; when it appears, war begins.

sentences.zh: 四填大而赤，可二丈，爲兵。

translations.literal: Sitian is large and red, about two zhang, and signifies armies.
translations.idiomatic: Sitian is great and red, about two zhang across, and portends warfare.

sentences.zh: 地維臧光星如月，始出，大而赤，去地二丈，東南，旱；

translations.literal: Diwei Zangguang Star is like the moon at first appearance, large and red, two zhang from the ground; in the southeast, drought;
translations.idiomatic: Diwei Zangguang Star resembles the moon at first rising, great and red, two zhang above the earth; in the southeast, drought;

sentences.zh: 西北，兵；

translations.literal: in the northwest, war;
translations.idiomatic: in the northwest, war;

sentences.zh: 出東北，大水。

translations.literal: in the northeast, great flood.
translations.idiomatic: in the northeast, great inundation.

sentences.zh: 老子星色白，爲善爲惡，爲饑爲凶，爲喜爲怒。

translations.literal: Laozi Star is white in color, bringing good and evil, famine and disaster, joy and anger.
translations.idiomatic: Laozi Star is white, bringing fortune and misfortune, hunger and calamity, joy and wrath.

sentences.zh: 營頭星有雲如壞山墜，所墜下有覆軍流血。

translations.literal: Banner Head Star has clouds like a crumbling mountain falling; beneath where it falls, armies are overthrown and blood flows.
translations.idiomatic: Banner Head Star is accompanied by clouds like a ruined mountain collapsing; where it falls, hosts are crushed and blood is shed.

sentences.zh: 積陵出西南，長三丈，主兵，小饑。

translations.literal: Jiling emerges in the southwest, three zhang long, presiding over armies and minor famine.
translations.idiomatic: Jiling appears in the southwest, three zhang in length, governing war and slight hunger.

sentences.zh: 昏昌出西北，氣青赤色，中赤外青，主國易政。

translations.literal: Hunchang emerges in the northwest, its qi green-red, red within and green without, presiding over change of government in the state.
translations.idiomatic: Hunchang appears in the northwest, its vapor green and red, red within and green without, governing the overturning of the realm's government.

sentences.zh: 莘星出西北，狀如環，大則諸侯失地。

translations.literal: Shen Star emerges in the northwest, ring-shaped; if large, feudal lords lose their lands.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Star appears in the northwest, shaped like a ring; if large, lords lose their territories.

sentences.zh: 白星如削瓜，主男喪。

translations.literal: White Star is like a trimmed melon and presides over mourning for men.
translations.idiomatic: White Star resembles a sliced melon and governs bereavement among men.

sentences.zh: 菟昌有赤青環之，主水，天下改易。

translations.literal: Tuchang is encircled by red and green and presides over flood; the realm is transformed throughout.
translations.idiomatic: Tuchang is ringed in red and green, governs inundation, and the empire is changed in all respects.

sentences.zh: 濛星赤如牙旗，長短四面，西南最多，亂之象。

translations.literal: Meng Star is red like a battle flag, long and short in the four directions, most numerous in the southwest—a sign of disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Star is red like a war banner, long and short across the four quarters, most frequent in the southwest—a token of chaos.

sentences.zh: 長星出西方。

translations.literal: The Long Star appears in the west.
translations.idiomatic: The Long Star appears in the west.

sentences.zh: 歲星之精，化爲天棓、天槍、天猾、天沖、國皇、及登，蒼彗。

translations.literal: The essence of the Year Star becomes Celestial Club, Celestial Spear, Celestial Mischief, Celestial Assault, Guohuang, Jideng, and the azure comet.
translations.idiomatic: Jupiter's essence transforms into Celestial Club, Celestial Spear, Celestial Mischief, Celestial Assault, Guohuang, Jideng, and the azure comet.

sentences.zh: 火星之精，化爲昭旦、蚩尤之旗、昭明、司危、天欃，赤彗。

translations.literal: The essence of the Fire Star becomes Zhaodan, the Banner of Chiyou, Zhaoming, Siwei, Celestial Interference, and the red comet.
translations.idiomatic: Mars's essence transforms into Zhaodan, the Banner of Chiyou, Zhaoming, Siwei, Celestial Interference, and the red comet.

sentences.zh: 土星之精，化爲五殘、六賊、獄漢、大賁、昭星、絀流、茀星、旬始、蚩尤，虹蜺、擊咎，黃彗。

translations.literal: The essence of the Earth Star becomes Wucan, Liuzzei, Yuhan, Daben, Zhaoxing, Chuoliu, Fei Star, Xunshi, Chiyou, rainbow, and Jijiu, and the yellow comet.
translations.idiomatic: Saturn's essence transforms into Wucan, Liuzzei, Yuhan, Daben, Zhaoxing, Chuoliu, Fei Star, Xunshi, Chiyou, rainbows, Jijiu, and the yellow comet.

sentences.zh: 太白之精，化爲天杵、天柎、伏靈、天敗、司奸、天狗、天殘、卒起，白彗。

translations.literal: The essence of the Great White becomes Celestial Pestle, Celestial Shaft, Hidden Spirit, Celestial Defeat, Si Jian, Celestial Dog, Celestial Ruin, and Sudden Rise, and the white comet.
translations.idiomatic: Venus's essence transforms into Celestial Pestle, Celestial Shaft, Hidden Spirit, Celestial Defeat, Si Jian, Celestial Dog, Celestial Ruin, Sudden Rise, and the white comet.

sentences.zh: 辰星之精，化爲枉矢、破女、拂樞、滅寶、繞綎、驚理、大奮祀，黑彗。

translations.literal: The essence of the Chronogram Star becomes Warped Arrow, Poniang, Fushu, Miebao, Raogeng, Jingli, and Dafensi, and the black comet.
translations.idiomatic: Mercury's essence transforms into Warped Arrow, Poniang, Fushu, Miebao, Raogeng, Jingli, Dafensi, and the black comet.

sentences.zh: 而月旁祅星，亦各有所生。

translations.literal: Malefic stars beside the moon also each have their source of origin.
translations.idiomatic: The malefic stars that appear beside the moon likewise each arise from their own source.

sentences.zh: 天槍、天荊、真若、天㨬、天樓、天垣，歲星所生也，見以甲寅日，有兩青方在其旁。

translations.literal: Celestial Spear, Celestial Jing, Zhenruo, Tianyao, Celestial Tower, and Celestial Enclosure are born of the Year Star; they appear on a jiayin day, with two green squares at their sides.
translations.idiomatic: Celestial Spear, Celestial Jing, Zhenruo, Tianyao, Celestial Tower, and Celestial Enclosure are engendered by Jupiter; they appear on jiayin day with two green squares at their sides.

sentences.zh: 天陰、晉若、官張、天惑、天雀、赤若、蚩尤，熒惑所生也，出在丙寅日，有兩赤方在其旁。

translations.literal: Tianyin, Jinruo, Guanzhang, Tianhuo, Tianque, Chiruo, and Chiyou are born of the Sparkling Deluder; they appear on a bingyin day, with two red squares at their sides.
translations.idiomatic: Tianyin, Jinruo, Guanzhang, Tianhuo, Tianque, Chiruo, and Chiyou are engendered by Mars; they appear on bingyin day with two red squares at their sides.

sentences.zh: 天上、天伐、縱星、天樞、天翟、天沸、荊彗，填星所生也，出在戊寅日，有兩黃方在其旁。
